Disclaimer: The below article is sponsored, and the views in it do not represent those of ZyCrypto. Readers should conduct independent research before taking any actions related to the project mentioned in this piece. This article should not be regarded as investment advice.

Hashi, Sui’s native Bitcoin finance infrastructure, is now live on mainnet — with more than 20 custody, retail, and DeFi participants on board, forming one of the broadest coalitions in Bitcoin finance to date.

Bitcoin has spent years becoming one of the world’s largest pools of capital. Now the infrastructure to put it to work has arrived. Supporting institutional and retail access are names including Anchorage Digital, Fluid, HoneyB, and Upshift — with BitGo, Inc. expected to follow in 2027.

The ecosystem continues to expand. Among the latest to join Hashi are Merkl, an onchain incentive platform, and Current, a lending protocol — additions that broaden the range of DeFi products and services being built around Bitcoin on Sui.

Hashi keeps Bitcoin on the Bitcoin network and mints hBTC — a 1:1 Bitcoin-backed asset — on Sui. That hBTC can then serve as collateral for lending, borrowing, and other onchain financial products.

Crucially, Hashi is decentralized by design. It’s secured by validators rather than any single entity, using industry-leading cryptography. On that foundation, it connects leading providers across custody, trading, and decentralized finance — giving Bitcoin holders a wide range of ways to put their assets to work.

With hBTC now live, Bitcoin holders have a new set of opportunities within reach — starting with borrowing against BTC and tapping new financial strategies through lending markets and vaults.

To meet the specific needs of institutions, several new providers are rolling out dedicated lending and vault facilities. Fluid’s institutional-grade lending protocol is now live on Sui, beginning with Bitcoin-backed stablecoin loans. Holders can use Hashi to bring BTC onto Sui as hBTC, then post it as collateral on Fluid to borrow stablecoins — starting with USDC, with more flows to come.

“Bitcoin is the largest pool of idle capital in crypto,” said Samyak Jain, founder and CEO at Fluid. “With Hashi, it can now power deep, capital-efficient credit markets on Fluid.”

For institutions, Hashi solves a key piece of the puzzle: custody. Institutions will be able to access Hashi through two leading crypto custodians — Anchorage Digital and BitGo, Inc. (“BitGo”) — giving them a clear path to hold or deploy BTC into Hashi.

Previously announced institutional partners, including Cumberland and Wave Digital Assets, will play roles as early participants — deploying BTC and stablecoins on Hashi and providing liquidity across a range of strategies on Sui.

On the DeFi side, Sui protocols including Blueprint Finance (Concrete), Bluefin, Cetus, Current, and Suilend will unlock new lending opportunities, stablecoin credit, and yield strategies — all backed by Bitcoin.

“Some of the world’s largest Bitcoin holders are sitting on enormous amounts of untapped financial potential,” said Nathan McCauley, CEO and Co-Founder at Anchorage Digital. “Hashi gives our institutional clients a new way to access Bitcoin finance on Sui, with their BTC held in custody at Anchorage Digital Bank.”

If you’re an institution interested in deploying BTC or stablecoins on Hashi, please reach out to your custodian or hashi@sui.io. Users can explore more at sui.io/hashi.

#5301. MIT Review Acclaims zk-SNARKs, but zk-STARKs May Steal the Show

Updated look back: this article revisits a 2018 story with what has happened since.

The short version: STARKs took a large share of the stage, SNARKs adapted, and Bulletproofs found a narrower job. Here is how the three compare and how the story played out.

A zero-knowledge proof lets you prove that a statement is true without showing the data behind it. MIT's examples were proving you are over 18 without giving your birth date, or proving you can afford a payment without showing your balance.

The idea is old. According to ethereum.org, it first appeared in a 1985 paper. What changed was that it became usable. MIT's entry, written by Mike Orcutt, credited much of that progress to Zcash, a currency launched in late 2016, and listed Zcash, JPMorgan Chase and ING as key players.

The same entry named two drawbacks. zk-SNARKs were slow and heavy to compute, and they needed a "trusted setup". It added that researchers were already looking for alternatives without those problems, but did not name any.

zk-SNARK stands for zero-knowledge succinct non-interactive argument of knowledge. "Succinct" is the selling point. Zcash's documentation says a proof is only a few hundred bytes and can be checked in a few milliseconds, even for a very large computation.

That is what makes shielded Zcash transactions possible. The transaction is encrypted on the blockchain, yet the network can still confirm that it follows the rules.

The cost is the setup. Early SNARKs needed a one-time ceremony that produced public parameters. The ceremony also produced secret randomness, and Zcash's own documentation says anyone who kept it could forge proofs and create counterfeit coins. Zcash ran two multi-party ceremonies, one for its Sprout version and one for Sapling, so that no single person held the secret. Users still had to trust that at least one participant destroyed their share.

The STARK paper, "Scalable, transparent, and post-quantum secure computational integrity", was submitted to the IACR ePrint archive on January 10, 2018 by Eli Ben-Sasson, Iddo Bentov, Yinon Horesh and Michael Riabzev. Its title states the three goals.

Transparent means no trusted setup. STARKs use public randomness, so there is no secret to leak.

Post-quantum refers to the underlying math. Ethereum.org explains that SNARKs depend on elliptic curve cryptography, which a future quantum computer may break, while STARKs rely only on collision-resistant hash functions.

Scalable means the work of checking a proof grows far more slowly than the computation being proved.

The trade-off is size. STARK proofs are larger, and ethereum.org notes that this makes them more expensive to verify on Ethereum. Figures quoted in the Ethereum Stack Exchange thread that cites this article give a sense of scale: about 288 bytes for a SNARK against about 45,000 bytes for a STARK in one comparison, and "hundreds of kilobytes" in one developer's real project. Those numbers depend heavily on the computation, so treat them as orders of magnitude.

Bulletproofs came out of Stanford in 2017, from Benedikt Bünz, Jonathan Bootle, Dan Boneh, Andrew Poelstra, Pieter Wuille and Greg Maxwell. Like STARKs, they need no trusted setup.

They were designed for one job: proving that a hidden amount in a confidential transaction falls within a valid range. The Stanford project page says they cut that proof from over 10 kB to under 1 kB. It also says a Bulletproof takes longer to verify than a SNARK, which is why they are not used for proving large computations.

Monero added Bulletproofs in its October 2018 network upgrade. Its documentation reports that average transaction size fell by at least 80 percent.

Partly. Three things happened after 2018.

STARKs reached production. Eli Ben-Sasson, the paper's first author, co-founded StarkWare with Alessandro Chiesa and Uri Kolodny. The company used STARKs first in StarkEx, a scaling service for individual clients, and then in Starknet, which launched its Alpha on Ethereum mainnet in November 2021. Starknet's documentation describes it as a permissionless validity rollup that settles on Ethereum using STARK proofs.

SNARKs fixed their own weakness. PLONK, published in August 2019 by Ariel Gabizon, Zachary Williamson and Oana Ciobotaru, is a universal SNARK: one setup can serve many different programs instead of one ceremony per program. Halo went further. Zcash says Halo removes the trusted setup entirely, and its Orchard shielded protocol, activated with the NU5 upgrade in May 2022, runs on the Halo 2 proving system.

That last point matters for the old "SNARKs need a trusted setup" comparison. It was accurate in 2018. It no longer holds for every SNARK.

The fair verdict: STARKs did not push SNARKs aside, but they did prove that transparency and hash-based security work at scale. The choice today is less about which family wins and more about what you need: the smallest proof, no setup, or protection against quantum attacks.

#5300. Bitwise CEO Urges Americans to Hold Crypto as Banking Giants Go Down

Following multiple technical outages at major U.S. banks that left thousands of people unable to access banking services or make transactions, Bitwise CEO Hunter Horsley has urged Americans to keep some of their funds in crypto or stablecoins as a backup plan.

In a recent X post, Horsley pointed to the weaknesses of traditional financial systems, especially in the context of the world's growing reliance on technology.

"Rolling bank outages in the AI era," he said.

"Consider having some stablecoins or crypto just in case."

Large U.S. financial institutions such as JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America and Wells Fargo experienced widespread complaints about technical outages on Nov. 16.

Customers said they were having trouble logging into their online accounts, viewing their balances and conducting transactions.

According to Fox News, the incident affected some of the biggest banking names in the U.S. Thousands of people reported the issue via the outage-tracking platform Downdetector.

Zelle, a popular payment service that people use in the U.S. to transfer funds between bank accounts, was also reportedly affected.

As of the evening of Nov. 16, Chase had fixed the technical issue, according to the bank. It said transactions were back to normal.

The outage reports initially pointed to multiple banking systems going down at the same time. But further investigation revealed that problems at Chase spilled over into transactions with other banks. However, the Zelle app itself continued to work.

Stablecoins such as USDT and USDC aim to track the value of the U.S. dollar as closely as possible. They can be an option for those looking to hold digital funds without the extreme price fluctuations of crypto assets like Bitcoin.

For instance, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, participants in blockchain networks can transfer dollar-based stablecoins 24/7. However, cashing them out into traditional money may still require access to traditional financial institutions.

XRP has finally printed a local reversal: the price is forming one higher high after another. There's a good chance this quick recovery turns into something more significant sooner than we anticipate. XRP is trading at $0.9927, up around 11% from the $0.89 low of the drop. The price is back at the $0.99 area, which was the August low.

Hopefully, bulls pick up the rally, though for now the momentum is slow. The descending volume on the price upside suggests fading. The divergence of moving averages is an anti-volatility signal right now rather than anything else. All of them still sit above the price, with the nearest one around $1.13.

Multiple indicators suggest a retrace, but the overall market picture is grim, to say the least. The worrying part is, ironically, the recovery of RSI, which is slowly moving above the oversold zone and opens up the way for an additional leg down. RSI is around 33 now, up from its low near 27.

The issue is the historic pattern XRP is forming: a constant downtrend with occasional recoveries that quickly turn into new breakdowns. In early November, XRP bounced from around $1.20 to the $1.30 area. The breakdown that followed took the price down by around 30% in under two weeks.

The downtrend is way stronger than the bullish reversal attempts XRP had earlier this month. Unfortunately, it can create a sustainable downtrend that can last for months, and considering XRP's price of $0.99, this is not something investors want.

The market is weak, and it might get weaker. The confirmation of a market recovery would only come if we witness specific signs of a bull run: higher highs and sustained buying.

#5298. Marathon Digital Cannot Stop Selling Bitcoin

Bitcoin mining giant MARA Holdings, formerly known as Marathon Digital, continues to offload its Bitcoin holdings, with another multimillion-dollar transfer spotted as the company's selling spree shows no signs of slowing down.

According to blockchain analytics platform Lookonchain, MARA transferred another 366 BTC, worth approximately $23.33 million, from its wallets on Nov. 18.

The latest transaction follows a series of substantial Bitcoin sales by the mining company throughout 2026.

Lookonchain estimates that MARA has already sold a staggering 40,581 BTC this year, generating approximately $3.03 billion at an average selling price of $74,446 per coin.

However, it remains unclear whether the latest 366 BTC transfer represents another completed sale or an internal movement of funds.

MARA's aggressive selling strategy is confirmed by its latest quarterly financial disclosures.

According to its Nov. 9 SEC filing, the company sold approximately 26,984 BTC for $1.9 billion during the first nine months of 2026.

Following the end of September, MARA liquidated another 13,597 BTC at an average price of approximately $81,039, raising an additional $1.1 billion.

These transactions bring its total disclosed Bitcoin sales to 40,581 BTC.

Notably, the company used $750 million from its latest sales to fully repay Bitcoin-backed loans, releasing 17,477 BTC previously pledged as collateral.

Interestingly, MARA has explicitly signaled that it intends to continue selling Bitcoin as part of a broader shift in its corporate strategy.

However, it began allowing sales of newly mined Bitcoin in 2025 before expanding the policy in 2026 to include coins already held on its balance sheet.

In its latest shareholder letter, MARA said it plans to continue monetizing Bitcoin to strengthen its financial flexibility.

The company specifically identified artificial intelligence infrastructure, upcoming convertible debt obligations and potential share repurchases as reasons for building up cash reserves.

The selling comes as MARA faces considerable pressure on its core mining business.

Third-quarter revenue declined 35% year over year to $164.2 million, compared to $252.4 million in the corresponding period of 2025.

#5297. NEAR’s Inflation Cut: The Math Behind a 5.27% to 3.37% Staking Yield

AI-assisted summary, reviewed by NullTX editors.

HSP-029 lowers NEAR’s issuance cap from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months. The cap formula, the epoch step and the yield math show what that does to stakers.

Most headlines on NEAR’s new inflation schedule stop at “2.5% to 1.6%.” Stakers feel a different number. They earn about 5.27% today and will earn roughly 3.37% once the cut finishes, and a single line of arithmetic accounts for the gap.

House of Stake ratified HSP-029 on November 16, after the Security Council’s 14-day veto window passed without a veto. The proposal touches one parameter, the maximum annual issuance rate, which drops from 2.5% to 1.6% over 24 months. It is the second cut in just over a year, coming after the October 2025 halving from 5%.

Everything else stays put. Issuance still splits 90% to staking participants and 10% to the protocol treasury. There is no new spending program, no validator subsidy and no automatic trigger that could push issuance back up. The full proposal models 11.8 million NEAR of issuance avoided over two years and 66.1 million over six, measured against leaving the cap at 2.5%.

The schedule is a straight line with no stair steps:

Here t is the number of months since the reduction begins. The 0.9% is the total drop (2.5 minus 1.6), and dividing it by 24 gives a monthly step of 0.0375 percentage points, or 3.75 basis points. The min(t, 24) term caps the ramp at month 24, and the cap sits at 1.6% from there on.

NEAR applies the step every epoch rather than once a month. An epoch lasts about 12 hours, so the cap slips by roughly 0.0006 percentage points each time, far too little to notice on any given day. There are no step dates to mark on a calendar. Sampled every six months, the line looks like this:

The yield column uses the math in the next section. It drops about 0.08 percentage points a month, evenly, with no cliff.

New tokens go mostly to stakers, so the staked pool splits the reward, and a smaller pool earns more per token. That gives a working formula:

gross yield ≈ 0.9 × issuance cap ÷ staking ratio

The 0.9 is the staker share of issuance. Using the proposal’s figures, 0.9 × 2.5% ÷ 0.4271 comes to 5.27%, where 42.71% is the staking ratio reported when the proposal went to vote. Put in the 1.6% cap and 0.9 × 1.6% ÷ 0.4271 gives 3.37%, the same number the proposal publishes. Anyone can check the headline yields on a calculator.

The formula has two limits. It uses the cap, but realized issuance runs a little lower because transaction fees are burned. HSP-029 measured 2.45% in September, which puts today’s yield near 5.16%. The staking ratio also moves. When more people stake, the same rewards spread over more tokens and yield falls further, and when people unstake it climbs. The 3.37% figure assumes today’s ratio holds.

Stakers feel it first. By the proposal’s own math, someone staking 1,000 NEAR ends up with about 20 fewer tokens after two years than if the cap had stayed at 2.5%. The numbers back that up: yield averages about 4.32% across the ramp, roughly 0.95 points under today’s rate for two years.

Holders who don’t stake come out ahead. More than half of NEAR’s supply sits unstaked, and every new token dilutes those holdings. Trimming the cap by 0.9 percentage points trims that dilution by the same amount each year. Stakers give up some reward so that everyone else gives up less value.

Validators get an easier path than in 2025, when the halving cut staking rewards from about 9% to 4.75% in a single upgrade. Operators now have 24 months to plan. NEAR’s analysis finds that most validator revenue comes from commission on delegated stake, so service quality and fee competition shape income more than the issuance rate does.

Recent history explains the setup. When the 2025 halving shipped, an earlier community poll had missed the two-thirds threshold, and critics said the core team pushed the change through anyway. HSP-029 sidesteps that argument by design.

Two separate approvals are required. Token holders voting through veNEAR set the direction, and that vote closed November 2 with 99.96% in favor and none against. Validators then decide on their own whether to adopt the protocol upgrade that makes the cap binding. The author, Sal Ternullo of SVRN, opened discussion on October 7, and the process ran through the Screening Committee and Security Council in public. Raising issuance again would take a new proposal and another round of validator adoption, so nothing can be added quietly later.

Ratification does not change issuance yet. A one-quarter grace period comes first, giving wallets, exchanges, custodians and staking providers time to update their disclosures. NEAR One then releases the upgrade and validators choose whether to adopt it, with the reduction starting about a quarter after ratification. On schedule, that means a start in early 2027 and a 1.6% cap around early 2029.

Three things are worth tracking. Validator adoption of the upgrade comes first, because the cap stays at 2.5% until enough validators run it. The staking ratio comes next, since it moves yield regardless of the formula. Last are the quarterly transparency reports NEAR has promised, which compare realized issuance with the schedule.

Price is a separate question. Lower issuance eases supply pressure, but nothing in it creates demand. The cap will follow its published line down, and yield will follow the cap.

#5296. Vitalik Buterin Wants Crypto to Be More Like Buying a House

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has said that crypto needs some of the features that made housing a safe investment for earlier generations. "We need the equivalent of those good properties that housing investment has, for modern digital assets," Buterin wrote in a post on X on Nov. 18.

The post came a day after economist Peter Tulip published his own post on housing in Raleigh, North Carolina. According to Tulip, looser zoning rules in the city set off a construction boom and pushed real rents down 15% between 2022 and 2025.

In his post, Buterin first pointed to a benefit of young people putting their savings into stocks and crypto instead of real estate.

"One benefit of younger generations investing more in stonks and other digital things instead of housing is that it reduces perverse incentives that drive people to push to keep housing expensive, instead of rejoicing when prices drop as we do for all other life necessities," he wrote.

Still, the Ethereum co-founder said that housing has had one advantage over stocks and crypto. He described it as "a culture and policy-encouraged default of investing in a safe non-crazy thing that you can't easily liquidate."

"Modern platforms encourage the opposite of this, leading to more irresponsible behavior," Buterin added.

Ether was trading at $1,808 on Wednesday.

Buterin has written about housing and urban planning before. He has supported the YIMBY movement for denser development in cities for several years.

In 2022, Buterin argued for a land value tax. According to him, such a tax would lower the upfront cost of buying a home and discourage speculation on vacant lots.

In 2025, the Ethereum co-founder called the housing market a "confusing market of peculiar NFTs." According to Buterin, what is really being sold under the label of square footage is the right to live in a particular city. At the time, he also said that legalizing dense development speeds up the economy and benefits even people who prefer single-family homes.

#5295. MEXC Announces Global Card Service Discontinuation

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. MEXC confirmed that its Global Card service will be discontinued on November 18, according to the exchange's announcement. The company cites service adjustments by its third-party card issuer. From the deadline, existing cards can no longer be used for transactions, and new card applications are suspended.

Users have two things to take care of before the service ends.

First, the remaining card balance has to be withdrawn: the Withdraw button on the Global Card page sends the funds to the Fiat account.

Second, subscriptions linked to the card should be cancelled or switched to another payment method. Unfortunately for cardholders, recurring payments will most likely fail if they stay on the old card.

If there's still a balance when the service ends, MEXC will credit it to the Spot account, so users will simply receive their funds back. It's important to keep in mind that pending card transactions need time to settle, which is why the balance snapshot comes on November 21, three days after the shutdown. The amount will be credited within three business days of the snapshot. Users do not need to take any action.

Refunds for previous card transactions will be credited to the Fiat account once MEXC receives them. Pending cashback will be credited automatically as scheduled. Elite VVIP users with zero-fee benefits will be refunded too, though the eligible fees return to their Spot accounts only before December 15.

Transaction history, card orders and cashback records stay available on the Global Card page for three months after the service ends, so it's worth saving anything needed before access ends.

Cryptocurrency services delegate certain types of services to third parties all the time, so witnessing a similar situation is more than a possibility here. Realistically, the shutdown is somewhat inconvenient rather than dangerous, as the balances are returned automatically. For users: stay vigilant and try not to put all your eggs in one basket.

Cardano-based stablecoin DJED has announced its sunset, as DJED and SHEN services will wind down on December 31, 2026, at 11:59 pm UTC.

DJED represents a crypto-backed, overcollateralized stablecoin protocol on Cardano whose US-dollar peg is maintained algorithmically against an ADA reserve (with SHEN as the reserve coin), rather than by fiat reserves.

"DJED and SHEN services will wind down at the end of December 31, 2026, at 11:59 pm UTC," a DJED-focused X account wrote.

ATTN: DJED & SHEN Holders DJED and SHEN services will wind down at the end of December 31, 2026 at 11:59pm UTC. Please redeem and convert any DJED and SHEN you hold before then. All redemptions are subject to the reserve ratio.

Users are urged to redeem and convert any DJED and SHEN they hold before this deadline. Users are to redeem on the protocol and convert their DJED and SHEN back to ADA on the official Djed page. Users who hold DJED or SHEN in liquidity pools, lending markets, or other DeFi platforms are urged to withdraw those positions first, then redeem or swap.

The Djed team said all systems are fully operational and redemptions are now open, subject to the reserve ratio. It further added that the Djed protocol will be maintained and remain available until December 31, 2026. After this date, all remaining funds will be allocated to the outstanding DJED/SHEN holders once the wind-down is complete.

Djed’s shutdown comes almost three years after its launch, which came in 2023. The stablecoin was officially launched on the Cardano mainnet on January 31, 2023, and was developed by COTI in collaboration with the Cardano ecosystem to be used on DeFi protocols on Cardano as a stable alternative to volatile cryptocurrencies.

In positive news for the Cardano ecosystem, Monument Bank Limited has launched tokenized deposits on the Midnight network, marking a milestone for the network and the decentralized finance ecosystem.

At present, Monument is the first UK bank to tokenize retail deposits on a public blockchain, offering clients a 5.2% AER fixed-term return on savings directly through its existing banking app, delivering institutional onchain finance through a familiar and user-friendly banking experience.

Up to £250 million of client deposits will be represented on Midnight in this opening phase, with deposits recorded one-to-one in sterling.

Bitcoin's 200-week moving average (200WMA) has climbed above $68,000 for the first time, Blockstream CEO Adam Back noted on X on Nov. 18. "Bitcoin passes $68k 200wma," he wrote. Back attached a 200-week moving average heatmap from Look Into Bitcoin, and the chart shows the indicator rising throughout Bitcoin's history. On Nov. 18, the indicator was between $67,955 and $68,145.

#bitcoin passes $68k 200wma https://t.co/dgIzS9Nsvw https://t.co/xzYdP0EvZh

Back is the cryptographer behind Hashcash. The algorithm laid the groundwork for proof-of-work, and Satoshi Nakamoto cited it in the Bitcoin white paper. Back was also one of the first people Satoshi contacted before the launch of Bitcoin in 2009.

The Blockstream CEO has posted about the 200WMA on X several times this year. On March 27, he wrote that the "200wma passes $59k." The indicator was just above $60,000 in early May, and on May 30, Back reported that it had crossed $61,000. In September, the 200WMA rose above $65,000 for the first time.

In a follow-up post in May, Back cited a maxim of the late Charlie Munger. According to Munger, an investor who buys only high-quality assets when they trade at the 200-week moving average would beat the S&P 500 over time. Back also noted that Munger and Warren Buffett never embraced Bitcoin.

In mid-September, Bitcoin was trading at around $76,000 to $77,000. At that time, the gap between the price and the 200WMA was more than $10,000.

On Wednesday, Bitcoin was trading at $64,150, about 6% below the 200WMA. On Nov. 15, BTC dropped as low as $62,000 before bouncing 5.5%. Back called the move "bouncy" in a post on X.

In a CNBC interview on Nov. 12, Back said that Bitcoin could reach $1 million by 2028. According to Back, more than 95% of potential institutional inflows into Bitcoin are still ahead. He named investment trusts, asset managers and corporate treasuries among the buyers, and he said that their buying was just beginning.

Back also pointed to the Bitcoin halving in the spring of 2028. He said that miners would sell fewer coins after it.

He made a similar point at Paris Blockchain Week in April. "When the Bitcoin price is low, the miners have to sell a bigger proportion… and when the price is higher, they don't have to sell as much," Back said at the time.

#5286. Bitcoin Price Crashes Below $62K: What Should You Do?

The CryptoNews editorial team is composed of seasoned writers specializing in cryptocurrency and blockchain technology. Their expertise ensures comprehensive, accurate, and insightful content for...

Bitcoin price has fallen below $62,000 for the first time since early July, extending a brutal November selloff as institutional investors pull billions from the market. BTC touched $61,270 just now, before recovering slightly to trade around $61,700.

Bitcoin price has now lost more than 10% over seven days, with selling pressure spreading across equities, precious metals and other risk assets. Yesterday’s $582.2 million outflow from US spot Bitcoin ETFs added another blow, bringing November withdrawals close to $3.5 billion.

BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) accounted for $541.1 million of Thursday’s withdrawals, its largest single-day outflow since launching. The same session saw $727 million in crypto liquidations, with bullish traders absorbing most of the damage.

Institutional demand is weakening, leveraged buyers are being forced out, and the Federal Reserve’s increasingly hawkish outlook is making speculative assets less attractive.

Bitcoin is now approaching $60,000, a level that could determine if the correction finds a floor or develops into something uglier.

The ETF withdrawals are arguably the biggest concern for Bitcoin holders right now. Spot Bitcoin ETFs became an important source of institutional demand after launching in January 2024. Their buying helped absorb available supply and gave traditional investors a regulated route into the market.

That demand is now moving in the opposite direction. US spot Bitcoin ETFs have lost more than $1.1 billion this week alone. November’s cumulative withdrawals have approached $3.5 billion.

The pressure extends beyond ETFs. Rising Treasury yields and expectations of another Federal Reserve rate increase in December have encouraged investors to reduce exposure to assets that offer no regular income.

Meanwhile, derivatives traders are taking heavy losses. CoinGlass data showed more than $700 million in liquidations across crypto markets over 24 hours. Long positions accounted for 86% of the total.

Bitcoin itself recorded nearly $202 million in liquidations, with bullish traders suffering the majority of forced closures.

This creates a difficult environment for buyers. Falling prices trigger liquidations, which create additional selling pressure and push prices lower. The reduction in open interest also suggests excessive leverage is being flushed from the market.

The immediate battle is around $60,000. Bitcoin needs to reclaim $62,000 and establish support above it before bulls can confidently argue that the latest breakdown was temporary.

Scenario 1: Bitcoin loses $60K and heads toward $58K or $53K.

This is the bearish outcome. A decisive break below $60,000 could trigger another wave of stop-loss orders and leveraged liquidations.

The next downside area sits around $58,000, while more aggressive technical projections point toward $53,700.

The daily chart offers little encouragement for bulls. Bitcoin trades below its major moving averages, while bearish momentum continues to dominate. A sustained recovery in ETF flows would become increasingly important to prevent further deterioration.

Scenario 2: Bitcoin stabilizes between $60K and $62K.

This would give buyers time to absorb available supply without immediately reversing the entire November decline.

The liquidation wave has already removed considerable leverage from the market. If ETF withdrawals begin slowing, Bitcoin could establish a trading range before attempting another recovery.

But sideways trading alone would not confirm a bottom. Buyers need to demonstrate that they can defend support through multiple sessions.

Scenario 3: Bitcoin reclaims $62K and launches a relief rally.

A recovery above $62,000 would provide the first meaningful sign that sellers are losing control. A move toward $65,000 would then become possible, followed by resistance around $68,000.

Consistent ETF inflows, improving market sentiment, and a weaker dollar would strengthen this scenario. Without those developments, any rebound risks becoming another opportunity for sellers to exit.

For existing holders, the decision depends heavily on their entry price, investment horizon, and exposure. Long-term holders who bought substantially below current prices have more room to withstand volatility. Selling simply because Bitcoin crossed a psychological threshold risks locking in profits or losses without knowing whether the broader investment thesis has changed.

However, investors holding leveraged positions face a different problem. Falling prices can trigger forced liquidations regardless of their long-term convictions. Reducing leverage and protecting available capital should take priority over waiting for a rebound.

For buyers, the temptation to buy the dip is understandable. Bitcoin is considerably cheaper than it was just weeks ago, but cheaper does not automatically mean undervalued.

Buying in stages rather than committing an entire allocation around $61,000 offers more flexibility if the market tests $58,000 or even $53,700.

Bitcoin price remains vulnerable to another leg down. The $60,000 level is no longer just a psychological milestone. It is where the next major battle between buyers and sellers.

#5285. Countdown to Upgrade: Only 4 Votes Needed for XRP Ledger Vault to Go Live in 2026

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. The Single Asset Vault amendment on the XRP Ledger is getting closer to activation on the mainnet as validator support builds for the network’s preparation to enable better DeFi functionality.

According to data from XRPScan, the SingleAssetVault amendment, or XLS-65, has received yes votes from 25 of 35 trusted validators, currently standing at 71.43% consensus as of November 18, 2026. It needs more than 80% of 35 votes (29) to start its 14-day countdown to activation. That means it needs four more votes to get there and could reach the magic number before the end of 2026.

The XRP Ledger’s amendment process requires a proposed amendment to be approved by more than 80% of trusted validators for 14 days before it is implemented. Validator support may shift during this time, and if the required 80% threshold is lost, activation may be delayed.

The Single Asset Vault amendment creates a structure for aggregating assets from multiple depositors and is intended to be used with the on-chain Lending Protocol. The amendment introduces a Vault object that defines the state of a tokenized vault, and the Vault entry is one of the ledger entry types it provides.

The Vault object holds important information such as available assets, shares, total value, and other relevant information. Users can create a Vault object with the VaultCreate transaction; the Vault object is tracked in an Owner Directory owned by the Vault Owner account.

The XRP Ledger lending amendment has gained additional yes votes. According to XRPScan, the LendingProtocolV1_1 amendment, also known as XLS-66, has received 24 yes votes out of 35 trusted validators, meaning it has 68.57% consensus as of November 18, 2026. It needs more than 80% of the 35 votes (29) to trigger a 14-day activation countdown.

This implies that there are five votes left for it to reach this threshold, with the possibility of it securing the required number of votes before the end of 2026 as well.

According to XRP enthusiasts, LendingProtocolV1_1 represents the biggest amendment for unlocking capital and liquidity on the XRP Ledger and is anticipated by institutional and retail users.

#5282. ‘More Secret’ Version of Bitcoin: Zcash (ZEC) Eyes Another Wall Street ETF

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. Asset manager Bitwise has filed an S-1 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission for a spot Zcash (ZEC) exchange-traded fund. The document appeared in the SEC's database on Nov. 17, 2026. On Wednesday, ZEC rose to $975 before it pulled back to around $927.

Zcash is often called a "more secret" version of Bitcoin. According to the S-1, the Zcash network supports two types of transactions, and the "shielded" ones use a form of zero-knowledge cryptography known as zk-SNARKs. Holders of shielded Zcash "may selectively disclose transaction information to third parties," the filing says.

Bitwise's fund will not use this feature. "The Trust does not engage in shielded transactions in connection with its activities," according to the document.

The shares are expected to list on the Dallas-based Texas Stock Exchange (TXSE) under the ticker ZEC. According to the S-1, Coinbase Custody Trust Company will act as the Zcash custodian, and BNY Mellon will serve as the cash custodian. Bitwise also wrote that "the Trust will not stake or otherwise seek to derive additional Zcash from its holdings." The sponsor fee in the filing is listed as "0.___% per annum."

In the risk section of the S-1, Bitwise wrote that "a number of digital asset trading platforms have delisted Zcash, restricted trading in Zcash or declined to support Zcash." According to the filing, many of these platforms cited regulatory or compliance concerns.

The platforms that still support Zcash "do so only with respect to transparent addresses and do not permit deposits or withdrawals to or from shielded addresses," the document says. Bitwise also pointed to new EU rules that take effect on July 10, 2027. According to the S-1, the rules will "prohibit credit institutions, financial institutions and crypto-asset service providers in the European Union" from keeping accounts in such assets.

Bitwise CIO Matt Hougan named Zcash one of his top three assets for the decade in September, alongside Bitcoin and tokenization projects. Three days before the S-1 filing, he called ZEC a "golden mean" between open Bitcoin and anonymous Monero in an interview.

Grayscale's Zcash fund (ZCSH) has traded on NYSE Arca since August 2026, and the Winklevoss brothers filed for their own Zcash ETF on Nasdaq in October. ZCSH held $496.79 million as of the Nov. 17 close, according to SoSoValue. The fund has attracted $168.76 million in net inflows since its launch, and it recorded no inflows on Nov. 17, when Bitwise filed its S-1.

#5280. XRP Ledger Scores Historic First in Global Banking Standards Review

XRP Ledger (XRPL) has marked a significant step in its journey to institutional adoption by becoming the first public permissionless layer-1 blockchain to see its principles of Architecture and Resiliency independently verified by the Global Layer One (GL1) Market Infrastructure Toolkit.

The foundation’s self-assessment was independently verified by the blockchain security firm CertiK on the responses and evidence submitted around the principles of Architecture and Resiliency.

The independent attestation report was released on Nov. 13, further strengthening the assertion of XRP Ledger's compliance with institutional financial infrastructure requirements.

This comes at a time when banks and asset managers are increasingly considering blockchain technology to enable tokenization of deposits, stablecoins, investment funds and other financial instruments.

The Global Layer One initiative is a collaborative effort between prominent financial institutions and policymakers to set standards for digital financial infrastructure.

Its main goal is to make cross-border transactions for tokenised assets seamless while ensuring that blockchain networks adhere to internationally expected standards for financial market infrastructure.

Interestingly, XRPLF self-assessed XRPL for all 10 principles.

CertiK independently verified it only for the principles of Architecture and Resiliency.

XRPLF also provided details on how requirements specific to private/permissioned networks are addressed by managing related risks for XRPL’s decentralized nature, open-source governance model, and protocol amendments.

XRP Ledger Foundation executive director Brett Mollin emphasized the need to give financial institutions tangible evidence instead of pitching ideas.

Mollin added that independent attestation from CertiK also gives financial institutions more confidence while vetting the network.

It does not mean that XRPL meets all the standards mentioned in the toolkit completely.

The XRP Ledger Foundation will continue to update its assessment in line with the development of GL1 principles and XRPL protocol amendments that are activated.

Nonetheless, it's another step towards XRPL's bid to be a possible infrastructure for regulated financial institutions looking for blockchain-based settlement and tokenization.

The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. The Hyperliquid Policy Center (HPC) sent a letter to the UK Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) on Nov. 18 with seven recommendations on the draft documents CP26/36 and GC26/7. Three of them concern CP26/36, and four concern GC26/7. The letter was signed by HPC chief executive Jake Chervinsky.

The UK's new crypto regime will start to apply on Oct. 25, 2027. The FCA opened its window for crypto license applications on Sept. 30, 2026, and the window will close on Feb. 28, 2027.

According to the letter, "Regulatory obligations belong with persons who have unilateral control over a function that is a regulated activity." HPC argued that attaching obligations to a person who could not discharge them "would offer consumers no additional protection."

In the letter, HPC also compared public blockchains with the internet. "Like a public blockchain, the internet depends on protocols that identifiable persons maintain and upgrade over time," the group wrote.

HPC asked the FCA to assess each participant in a blockchain network separately. Proprietary traders and market makers "supply much of the liquidity on which order books depend," the group wrote. HPC also asked the regulator to describe compliance requirements as outcomes and to hold regulated firms accountable for them.

On Aug. 24, HPC urged the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) to harmonize their rules for perpetual contracts. The group argued that such products should be classified by their economic structure. According to HPC, a harmonized framework would let exchanges compete on "execution quality and liquidity."

On Sept. 30, HPC sent its response to the European Union's review of the MiCA rules. In it, the group asked the EU to treat crypto perpetual futures as derivatives under MiFID II. "Clarity in application, rather than new legislation, is what would assist in regulating perpetual futures," HPC wrote at the time.

Chervinsky previously served as chief policy officer at the Blockchain Association and as chief legal officer at the crypto venture firm Variant.

#5271. Gonka AI Hit by $1 Million Exploit as Hacker Drains Stablecoins

Decentralized artificial intelligence (AI) network Gonka AI has reportedly suffered a massive security attack in which hackers exploited its Ethereum bridge to withdraw stablecoins and issue unbacked tokens worth over $1 million.

According to blockchain analytics firm Onchain Lens, the hacker was able to gain access to the bridge's BLS group key, allowing the attacker to withdraw funds and issue Wrapped Gonka (WGNK) tokens without backing them with the required assets.

Per the report, the hacker managed to withdraw $884,800 in Tether (USDT) and USD Coin (USDC) stablecoins and also issued $172,000 in unbacked WGNK tokens.

Combined, the total value of the affected assets stood at around $1.06 million, per Onchain Lens.

Following the hack, the funds were transferred through the decentralized exchange Uniswap and multiple crypto wallets, making it challenging to trace their final destination.

The attack targeted Gonka AI's cross-chain bridge. The cross-chain bridge makes it possible to transfer assets from Gonka AI's native chain to Ethereum and vice versa.

According to the project's technical documentation, withdrawing funds from Gonka to Ethereum requires certain cryptographic signatures from the network's validator set.

The cryptographic signatures are checked against the BLS group key, which changes with every network epoch.

Per the report, the attacker was able to change the epoch BLS group key on the bridge, making it possible for the hacker to control the part of the bridge responsible for authorizing fund withdrawals.

Thus, the hacker was able to withdraw funds from the bridge's stablecoin reserves and issue WGNK tokens without locking the required amount of assets on the native blockchain.

Blockchain security firm Blockaid noted that the hack had taken place, with the total amount of funds stolen reaching about $1.05 million across roughly five transactions at the time of the initial alert.

At the time it spotted the suspicious activity, Blockaid noted that the hack was still ongoing.

Onchain Lens's numbers differ slightly, with the firm reporting around $884,800 in stablecoin withdrawals and $172,000 in unbacked WGNK issuance.

Notably, the issuance of unbacked tokens presents an additional problem, given that such tokens could potentially enter circulation without the necessary reserves to back them.

#5268. 178 Websites Infected in Major Optimizely Hack: Crypto Wallets Targeted, but Bitcoin Barely Reacted

Optimizely attack infects 178 websites, steals crypto and card data, and exposes users to wallet-address swaps and iPhone exploits.

An Optimizely attack on Monday, November 16, planted crypto-stealing code on the websites of 178 organizations, including Ledger, HSBC, Zoom, the BBC and CNN. The malicious script swapped crypto wallet addresses, skimmed card numbers, and tried to break into iPhones for about 19 hours before it was cleaned up.

BREAKING: A cyberattack hit 178 major organizations, including Zoom, CNN, BBC, Fox News, HSBC, Ledger, Equifax, Salesforce, IKEA and Air France-KLM, by loading malware on the Optimizely Web platform, exposing visitors to scripts built to steal payment data and exploit iOS…

— The Hormuz Letter (@HormuzLetter) November 17, 2026

Optimizely is a tool companies use to test different versions of their web pages. An attacker slipped code into the scripts it serves, so every site that loaded them ran the malware.

We traced the attacker’s Bitcoin wallet. It received five payments worth about $5,500, and one victim alone sent nearly 90% of it. Bitcoin barely moved while the attack ran.

So what happened, and what is the real impact of hacks like this one?

Security researcher Scott Helme of Report URI found the code and published a full breakdown. The attacker wrote it into a settings field in customers’ Optimizely projects, so it was served from Optimizely’s own servers and looked legitimate.

Optimizely said it “secured affected user accounts and added protections against further unauthorized code delivery.” Report URI found no sign that Ledger hardware wallets themselves were breached. The danger was on the website, where a copied address could be swapped before a user pasted it.

Report URI listed the attacker’s wallets. We checked the Bitcoin one on mempool.space, the public Bitcoin block explorer.

The Optimizely attack’s impact was tiny, and the market ignored it. Bitcoin is near $64,300 after its weekend low of $62,006, and that slide came from wider selling, not this attack.

These attacks hit users where no wallet setting can protect them. The fix is on the user’s side: check the address on the hardware wallet’s screen before signing, send a small test transfer first, and keep phones updated.

#5267. CZ Sounds Alarm as Japan Orders Crackdown on ID Data Storage

Binance founder Changpeng Zhao, widely known as CZ, has expressed his concerns about the storage of sensitive personal data after Japanese authorities called on rental car services to delete customers' identity documents following a massive data breach.

In his latest X post, CZ pointed to a Nov. 18 notice issued by Japan's Personal Information Protection Commission (PPC). The notice urges rental car services to be cautious about unnecessarily storing images of driver’s licenses and other government-issued identification documents.

The recent call by Japanese authorities comes after a massive cybersecurity attack on a popular Japanese car-sharing service called Times Car, operated by Park24 Group.

The incident began when the company noticed suspicious activity on its system on Sept. 25. As a result, it launched an investigation into whether someone had accessed its systems without permission, potentially exposing customer data.

As per the disclosure by Park24 on Oct. 23, about 6.63 million customer accounts were impacted by the breach.

Worse, the investigation uncovered evidence that hackers had transmitted 1,464,800 encrypted images of identification documents, including driver’s licenses, to external locations.

Besides that, another 891,602 encrypted images of identification documents were accessed suspiciously. However, investigators found no evidence that these additional ID images had been transmitted outside the company’s systems.

Japan’s Personal Information Protection Commission issued its notice on Nov. 18, focusing on the risks of retaining sensitive personal data even after its original purpose has been fulfilled.

The regulatory body stressed that storing unnecessary identification images could significantly worsen the consequences of cyberattacks.

Although Japan’s latest warning specifically targets the rental car industry, CZ’s decision to share his concerns about this issue also raises questions about personal data protection in the crypto industry.

Generally, centralized crypto exchanges require users to go through a Know Your Customer (KYC) process to access their trading platforms.

Depending on the platform and jurisdiction, these processes may require users to provide photos of their passports, driver’s licenses, national ID cards, and other sensitive information.

This kind of sensitive data can be a goldmine for cybercriminals, who can exploit stolen personal information for various activities such as identity theft, phishing attacks, fraudulent registrations, and more

Russia has finally opened its crypto market for retail customers as its central bank today enabled trading in Bitcoin, Ethereum, and USDT for the general public. With the law signed by President Vladimir Putin, the Bank of Russia officially rolled out BTC, ETH, and USDT for public trading on domestic exchanges, beginning Nov. 17, 2026.

The new regulation, announced by the Bank of Russia last week, took effect today, Nov. 17. The move allows individual customers to purchase these assets through intermediaries, including brokers, exchanges, and authorized crypto marketplaces. This means ordinary investors can now buy up to 300,000 rubles ($3,700) in a year through a single broker, exchange, or asset manager, after passing a mandatory test.

The announcement expands access to regulated crypto trading in the country and connects the assets with TradFi. This allows non-qualified investors to buy and trade BTC, ETH, and USDT directly through traditional exchanges and clearing systems.

However, qualified investors are not subject to such asset limits and trading restrictions.

The development points out that Russia has taken decisive action to deepen the integration of the crypto market with traditional finance. The debut indicates surging retail interest in cryptocurrency amid regulatory evolution.

It signals a strategic shift in how traditional exchanges handle digital assets. Accommodating retail clients signals growing confidence in the crypto market’s maturity. This highlights rising demand for coordinated exposure to crypto assets within Russia’s capital markets.

The announcement introduces new entry gateways that give retail investors organized access to the crypto market, redefining how these assets are traded locally and internationally.

In the past, crypto in Russia operated in a highly restrictive, complex regulatory environment.  Now, the regulator is moving toward a balance between investor freedom and financial stability. In July, the central bank opened the door to crypto for companies to facilitate global trade. This month, it introduced new legislation that allows retail investors to trade crypto within specified limits.

#5262. Can AI Hack Smart Contracts? How AI Agents Are Changing Blockchain Security

Smart contract vulnerability scanners typically work by looking for certain patterns. However, because an AI agent can iterate and make use of dependencies, local blockchain forks, and decompilation, it weakens the protection gained by keeping source code secret, and can attempt attacks against complex vulnerabilities such as access control bugs, accounting errors, oracle-related bugs and unexpected contract interactions.

For example, in December 2025, Anthropic released results from SCONE-bench, a smart contract benchmark of 405 contracts that were exploited in the 2020 - 2025 period. They were able to reproduce exploits for 207 contracts, totalling $550.1 million (simulated stolen funds).

To make sure the agent was not simply memorising exploits that were already published, newer vulnerabilities that had been published after their training cutoff were tested on Claude Opus 4.5, Sonnet 4.5, and GPT-5, which were able to generate $4.6 million (simulated stolen funds).

Finally, they analysed 2,849 recent smart contracts with no known issues, discovering two previously unknown vulnerabilities that could have resulted in $3,694 (simulated stolen funds), emphasising the ability of AI agents to discover new vulnerabilities rather than simply exploiting known ones.

Anthropic emphasised that no actual funds were lost during these experiments. It should also be noted that in one of their experiments using GPT-5, it cost $3,476 for API usage, which leaves a slim (simulated) profit.

With automated hacking becoming more effective, how can we be sure that DeFi will be able to stay ahead of these AI agents? Hacken, a blockchain security firm, reported that $1.18 billion was lost in 107 crypto hacks during the third quarter of 2026. 48% of this was from exploiting smart contracts.

Of course, this doesn’t specify the cause of these hacks. Regardless, it emphasises the importance of being able to stay ahead of AIs which could be used for exploitation.

Chainalysis estimates that approximately $36.7 million was stolen in 2026 from DeFi protocols that had not undergone smart contract verification. It also notes AI-assisted reverse engineering as an emerging risk without attributing any particular thefts to AI.

In an experiment by a16z on 20 past DeFi price manipulation exploits, apparent success rates of 50% were reduced to 10% when the researchers restricted access to transactional data that revealed the original exploit. When the researchers gave the AI some high-level information about the DeFi domain, success rates jumped to 70%.

In February 2026, OpenAI and Paradigm released a benchmark for evaluating agents’ abilities in the domains of vulnerability detection, patching, and exploitation using an EVM environment (EVMbench). Results showed that GPT-5.3-Codex achieved a 71% success rate in exploitation (limited to a sandboxed environment) and 33.3% for GPT-5.

In October 2026, CyberChainBench was released, analyzing 541 exploit events across 9 Ethereum-compatible blockchains. The best-performing configuration achieved 37.5%, 43.7%, and 23.4% success rates for detection, exploitation, and patching respectively.

In a simulation, the best-performing agent profited $57.4 million from exploits on 200 exploit events that occurred after the cutoff. Some of the reported high-severity issues were evaluated and determined to not be exploitable by OpenZeppelin. Since much of the data is trained on in the public, results may be exaggerated.

Agents will continue to improve, and while current results are not an indication that AI-driven agents are responsible for large scale on-chain thefts, it is an indication that AI can find and exploit weaknesses in smart contracts given a certain environment. Given the ease with which agents can try attacking many different protocols, smaller protocols may see an uptick in exploit attempts.

Teams that implement rigorous testing and monitoring could have an edge over other teams. For example, AI could be used to test a contract prior to deployment, generate regression tests, and identify weird behavior on-chain. A human would still need to verify any potential issues and sign off on changes.

Teams should continue to perform third-party audits and implement other security best practices such as limiting access to sensitive information, setting up alerts and response plans, restricting the amount of money in a wallet, making sure AI systems do not have permissions to transact without human oversight where necessary, and so on.

#5258. XRP Flashes Biggest Volatility Warning Among Major Cryptocurrencies

XRP stands out as the cryptocurrency with the most alarming volatility warning among major digital assets, according to recent Coinbase data. The options market indicates that traders are now preparing for price swings that could be nearly double XRP's historical seven-day price move.

XRP's seven-day options-implied price move stands at 1.94 times its historical median. This figure far exceeds similar metrics for major cryptocurrencies such as Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH) and Solana (SOL).

XRP exhibits the highest premium above its own historical volatility. Solana shows the lowest premium among these four cryptocurrencies, Coinbase remarked.

As the chart below indicates, the options-implied seven-day price move for XRP is around 9.6%, according to Glassnode and Coinbase data as of Nov. 17. This compares to its historical median absolute price move of about 4.9%.

Basically, this means that the options market is signaling a price swing nearly twice as large as XRP's typical seven-day price movement.

Interestingly, Solana's implied price move is also close to 9.5%, almost the same as XRP's. Yet its historical median weekly price move is much higher at about 6.5%.

The key here is that although both cryptocurrencies exhibit similarly large potential price moves, the magnitude of the expected volatility surprise is significantly greater for XRP relative to its usual trading range.

For comparison, Bitcoin shows an options-implied seven-day move of about 6%, versus its historical median of about 3.5%. For Ethereum, these numbers are about 8% and 5.1%, respectively.

Obviously, this latest figure doesn't necessarily imply that XRP is going to crash. It's a sign that options traders expect a big price move regardless of its direction.

Implied volatility is a forward-looking measure. It's based on options prices. The higher the implied volatility, the more traders pay for exposure to potential price movements or protection against them.

The chart from Coinbase is based on a one-standard-deviation estimate. It's derived by converting annualized at-the-money implied volatility into a seven-day timeframe.

For XRP, the roughly 9.6% implied move represents a statistical range. It's not a guaranteed price target. A one-standard-deviation range suggests about a 68% chance of the price staying within this range under typical modeling assumptions.

Thus, the latest figure of 1.94x implies that XRP's volatility premium remains high despite a slight decrease from the previous reading.

From XRP traders' perspective, this can be a very challenging market environment. For traders using leverage, there could be a high risk of liquidation due to potentially sharp price moves.

#5253. 17 Years Ago, Satoshi Nakamoto Opens His BitcoinTalk Account: What Happened Next

On this day, 17 years ago, Satoshi Nakamoto opened an account on BitcoinTalk, the place that would become the home of early Bitcoin enthusiasts and then turn into a public forum for crypto in general, until social media platforms took over the internet.

The network itself was barely 1 year old, and its future raised more questions than answers. Satoshi Nakamoto welcomed users on the forum and invited any questions people had regarding the cryptocurrency.

In 2010, the revolution began: 10,000 BTC was used to buy two pizzas, one of the first uses of the digital asset in exchange for a commodity. In May, Laszlo Hanyecz probably had the most expensive pizza dinner in history, considering how much BTC rallied after that. By December, Satoshi made their final BitcoinTalk post and announced their farewell.

The 2011-2014 period turned out to be the foundation for the network as a whole. Bitcoin became an open-source project maintained by others. The first halving happened in November 2012 and reduced the block issuance from 50 to 25 BTC per block.

The first-ever exchange implosion, Mt.Gox in 2014, raised serious questions about the security and stability of centralized exchanges, an issue we haven't solved 17 years later.

2017-2021 were the years when the industry truly blossomed. We had our first bull run on Bitcoin, which pushed the price above expected levels, to almost $20,000 in December 2017, along with the first altcoin bull run and the birth of new technologies like smart contracts, NFTs and many more. The next cycle took Bitcoin to around $69,000 in November 2021.

However, with the growth of the industry, multiple conflicts arose around safety, integrity and usage. The first country in the world to adopt Bitcoin was El Salvador, which implemented the digital currency as a true means of payment, in addition to accumulating it in its treasury.

2022 was the pivotal year, marked by the FTX and Terra crashes that changed how investors treat markets in general. FTX wasn't just an exchange: it was the backbone of the cryptocurrency market in those years. It aimed to rival Binance and become the bridge between institutional investors and crypto.

However, poor risk management, issues with fund allocation and many other factors caused an implosion that ended the bull run.

In 2024, Wall Street arrived in crypto with ETFs, ETPs, perpetual futures and a regulatory framework. The digital assets industry became a part of a larger market. Whether that is good or bad is a question to consider, but one thing is clear: Bitcoin has come a very long way since 2010 and is evolving to this day.

The next step is the arrival of AI and rising cybersecurity risks, which go toe-to-toe with the quantum danger. How the first cryptocurrency handles them is a question that directly affects its future.

Total crypto market capitalization dropped 1.3% over the past 24 hours to $2.253 trillion, with Bitcoin (BTC) falling 1.5%, the most among the other top 10 biggest cryptos. Bitcoin is currently trading at $63,585.

Anthropic has expanded its IPO to 980 million shares, up from the initially planned 825 million, following exceptionally strong demand from institutional and retail investors.

Reported strategic investors include Nvidia, Microsoft, Google, AMD, Broadcom, Micron and TSMC. Combined, the public offering and private placement are expected to generate more than $107 billion.

Anthropic’s IPO could have implications for crypto markets beyond the AI sector. The listing also gives retail investors a direct way to bet on AI, potentially reducing demand for crypto-native AI tokens that have attracted investors seeking similar exposure.

Major crypto exchange Coinbase shared the options-implied seven-day ratios for major cryptocurrencies, highlighting that options traders might be preparing for an unusually large price move for XRP.

In an X post, Coinbase Markets shared the outcome of dividing the options-implied 7-day move by the median 7-day move for XRP, Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana.

Options-implied 7d move, divided by each asset's own median 7d move: $XRP 1.94× $BTC 1.69× $ETH 1.56× $SOL 1.46× $XRP is priced furthest above its own history, $SOL the least. Which one is asking for more than its own history delivered? https://t.co/WgWbqjcgwI

This suggests how much movement options markets are pricing in relative to each asset's own historical behavior. However, it does not compare their expected dollar or percentage moves directly.

According to the figures shared by Coinbase, XRP's options-implied seven-day move stands at 1.94 times its own historical median seven-day move. Bitcoin follows at 1.69 times, while Ethereum records 1.56 times and Solana comes in at 1.46 times.

XRP, therefore has the highest relative reading among the four assets, suggesting options traders are pricing in a more pronounced move than the token has typically delivered over a comparable period.

At the time of writing, XRP was down 1.93% in the last 24 hours to $0.98 amid the continued profit-taking in the market. XRP briefly reached $1 on November 18, 2026, but fell afterwards as traders took profits. XRP is down 21.57% so far in November, but its history says more than its current price action does.

XRP’s average November gain is skewed upward by massive outlier rallies—specifically +550% in 2013 and +282% in 2024. Its median November return is about -10%, meaning it has closed lower in most cycles in history. XRP dropped roughly 23.42% in November 2019 and lost 12.18% in November 2025 (opening at around $2.51 and closing at around $2.20).

A weak November doesn’t always mean a weak December: for instance, after falling 9.1% in November 2015, XRP jumped 46.8% in December 2015.

In the near term, XRP’s price recovery will target $1 before moving to the $1.24–$1.26 range. Alternatively, if the price falls further, it is likely to find support at $0.89.

The same pattern, he said, unfolded ahead of Anthropic’s offering. After SpaceX completed its listing, crypto markets staged a notable rebound. Garlinghouse expects a similar bounce this time.

Anthropic, the artificial-intelligence company behind the Claude chatbot family, has priced its IPO at $83 per share, above the previously marketed range of $70 to $78.

The deal ranks among the largest IPOs in history, raising tens of billions of dollars and valuing the company in the trillion-dollar range, and shares are set to begin trading on Nasdaq under the ticker ANT.

Such blockbuster offerings typically attract enormous institutional and retail interest, temporarily diverting capital from other risk assets. Once the primary allocation is complete and secondary-market trading stabilizes, some of that capital often flows back into crypto and other liquid markets.

Bitcoin had slipped near $62,000 on Wednesday before recovering above $63,000 early Thursday. Garlinghouse framed the dip as a temporary capital-rotation effect rather than a fundamental loss of confidence in digital assets. He also expressed confidence that Anthropic’s shares would trade strongly given the strong demand and pricing above the range.

Looking further ahead, Garlinghouse remained optimistic about blockchain’s long-term role. He predicted that within roughly a decade, blockchain technology will be deeply embedded across global financial infrastructure, much as artificial intelligence has already transformed multiple industries.

His comments highlight how large technology IPOs can create short-term pressure on crypto while potentially reinforcing longer-term narratives around innovation and capital markets.

On Nov. 18, Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) added the decentralized exchange Hyperliquid to its list of suspicious virtual asset trading platforms. The listing covers the web interface of the Hyperliquid trading terminal at app.hyperliquid.xyz/trade. The HYPE token dropped to around $65.50 on the evening of Nov. 18, and it recovered to $68.79 by midday Nov. 19, according to TradingView data.

According to the entry, the company claims to provide digital asset trading services on the website, and it has no address on record. Hyperliquid is not licensed by the SFC, and it is suspected of operating a virtual asset trading platform in Hong Kong or actively promoting its services to the public, the regulator said.

In an accompanying warning, the SFC reminded investors that such platforms often lure users with "incredible investment opportunities." The SFC also reminded investors that clients of unlicensed platforms have no legal protection if a platform is hacked or misappropriates their assets.

On the same day, the Hyperliquid Policy Center (HPC) sent a letter to the U.K. Financial Conduct Authority with seven recommendations on the country's new crypto rules. "Regulatory obligations belong with persons who have unilateral control over a function that is a regulated activity," the group wrote.

On Nov. 16, two days before the SFC added Hyperliquid to the list, Hong Kong Financial Secretary Paul Chan spoke at the Bloomberg Global Regulatory Forum. "Before the end of this year, we will introduce a bill to complete the regulatory perimeter," Chan said.

According to Chan, the bill will cover crypto dealers, custodians, advisers and asset managers. "Decentralisation does not mean less accountability," he said.

In April, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority licensed HSBC and Anchorpoint Financial as the first stablecoin issuers in the city, out of 36 applicants in the first round.

#5244. Trading Bots No Longer a Niche: Now It’s Web3’s Default

Home » Exchanges » Trading Bots No Longer a Niche: Now It’s Web3’s Default

AI-powered trading tools are gradually becoming the default interface for Web3 trading, new research reveals.

A new report from Bitrue Research Institute tracks how trading bots have shifted from specialist software for technical users into everyday infrastructure across crypto markets.

The research paper combines public GitHub data on open-source projects, a survey of Bitrue users, and profiles of eight active bots to show where automation is heading.

Public GitHub activity shows a clear change in focus. New repositories describing themselves as “trading agents” jumped from 110 in 2024 to 1,133 in 2025 and reached 6,121 through November 15, 2026, more than five times the prior year’s total.

Classic crypto trading bot projects also grew sharply, rising from 551 in 2024 to 2,399 in 2025 (a 4.4× increase) with another 2,948 created so far in 2026.

The longest-running open-source tools still dominate stars: Freqtrade (56,933), Hummingbot (21,231), Jesse (8,807), and OctoBot (6,951).

An industry survey of 3,708 crypto traders published by MEXC in October 2026 found that 84.8% had used AI for research or trading in the previous six months, with 53.1% doing so at least weekly.

🤖 Here are more ways to earn with #BitrueAI!With #BitrueAI, select from a list of #crypto like #Bitcoin, #Solana and #XRP🔸 30 days backtested results🔸 Choose your own grid direction🔸 Customize your own settings with #BitrueAI👉 Start Now: https://t.co/3PW15XTAvd pic.twitter.com/ohHDBirMmQ

Among AI users, 34.6% had used an exchange’s own strategies or bots and 17.1% had connected an external agent.

On one major multi-exchange platform, average daily bot launches rose 29% from July to September 2026, reaching 862 per day, with real-fund launches up 36% and DCA bots up 80%.

The report identifies five structural changes:

In Bitrue’s survey of users who had not yet tried an AI trading bot, concern about losses and risk control was the top reason for hesitation (45.5%). Other common reasons included not trading futures yet (27.3%) and simply not knowing the feature existed (22.7%).

Willingness to let AI trade rose from 55% when only notifications were offered to 71.8% when limits on funds, positions, leverage, and losses were in place. Only 6.5% of respondents said they would allow AI to control more than half their account.

Among non-users, the most requested first steps were a clearer explanation of what the bot does (27.3%) and a trial reward for the first trade (22.7%). Half of those who had not tried an AI bot said they were ready to do so; another 36.4% wanted to learn more first.

Users who had already tried Bitrue AI most often cited time saved from watching charts, automatic execution, and market analysis as the main benefits. Requests for improvement centered on more trading pairs, flexible parameters & alerts tied to indicators such as RSI.

The report profiles eight systems that illustrate different approaches:

AI automation continues to expand, but adoption still hinges on control. Crypto traders want to see why a strategy was chosen, know the maximum loss, test it first, and understand connection security and costs.

Tools that explain their reasoning, enforce user-set boundaries, and allow small or reversible starts are the ones positioned to convert interest into regular use. The report does not forecast specific outcomes beyond these observed trends.

The numbers show both rapid builder activity and cautious but growing trader demand. The gap between the two is being closed by guardrails, explanations, and simpler interfaces rather than by handing full control to AI.

Binance will delist five crypto spot trading pairs within the next 24 hours on Nov. 20, 2026, following a review.

To protect its users and to ensure a high-quality trading market, Binance conducts regular reviews of all listed spot trading pairs; it may delist certain spot trading pairs for various reasons, including low liquidity and trading volume.

Binance will delist GAS/TRY, HBAR/BNB, HIVE/TRY, KSM/TRY and ZAMA/TRY pairs on November 20, 2026 at 03:00 UTC, according to an official announcement published on November 18.

Four of the five affected pairs are related to the Turkish lira (TRY), while the last one is HBAR/BNB. The decision affects trading between these specific assets and does not mean the cryptocurrencies themselves are being completely delisted from Binance.

The exchange clarified that users will still be able to trade the affected tokens through other available spot trading pairs on its platform.

Binance will terminate Spot Trading Bots services for the spot trading pairs simultaneously where applicable. Users are strongly advised to update and/or cancel their Spot Trading Bots prior to the cessation of services for Spot Trading Bots to avoid any potential losses.

In related news, Binance Margin will initiate a routine cleanup of Cross Margin accounts with collateral valued at less than 1 USD (or equivalent in other assets), effective from November 30, 2026 at 00:00 (UTC). The cleanup will be executed on a daily basis as an ongoing operational process.

Affected accounts include Cross Margin Accounts with a collateral value of less than 1 USD equivalent across all assets and no outstanding liabilities, as well as Margin Accounts with no capital activity in the past 6 months. Capital activity refers to any action that generates a capital flow.

For each eligible Small-Asset Account, the system will automatically transfer the collateral in users’ Margin Accounts to their Spot Accounts while the Margin Account functions remain normal, allowing users to transfer, borrow, or trade at any time after the cleanup.

Accounts with collateral equal to or exceeding 1 USD equivalent are not affected by this cleanup.
