#5202. Eight Years: From a Crypto Exchange to a Global Ecosystem Serving 40 Million Users

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

What started eight years ago as a cryptocurrency exchange has evolved into an international business ecosystem of 11 companies serving approximately 40 million users worldwide. As WhiteBIT celebrates its eighth anniversary and W Group marks its first year, the milestones highlight a transformation from a single trading platform into a diversified business connecting traditional finance, digital assets, and emerging technologies.

The scale of this growth is reflected in WhiteBIT’s $2.8 trillion trading volume in 2026 and more than 5,500 institutional clients. Meanwhile, W Group has expanded from eight to 11 companies in one year, growing its combined user base from 35 million to approximately 40 million.

Established in 2025, W Group brought together businesses developed around WhiteBIT under a broader strategy: connecting traditional finance and digital assets while extending their applications into new industries.

The group aims to build more than a portfolio of independent companies. By combining financial infrastructure, technology and expertise, its businesses can develop new services, reach new markets and create opportunities across industries.

In 2026, W Group expanded well beyond financial services. Dutch sports car manufacturer Spyker joined the group in June, opening opportunities to apply digital finance and blockchain technology to luxury automotive.

W Group has also made a $400 million investment commitment in SignSplit, the signed-data platform for the AI era. The seed round values SignSplit at $1 billion.

In banking, Georgia-based hashbank, a fully licensed digital bank, combines traditional banking services with cryptocurrency functionality, allowing customers to manage fiat and digital assets within one environment.

Together, these businesses illustrate W Group’s strategy of connecting financial services, technology, and consumer-facing products into an ecosystem where each company can contribute to the growth of the others.

WhiteBIT remains a central pillar of W Group, providing trading infrastructure and digital asset services for retail and institutional clients.

In 2026, the exchange recorded $2.8 trillion in trading volume, with derivatives generating approximately $3.5 billion in daily activity. Its platform now offers nearly 1,200 trading markets.

Trading conditions have also improved. Spot trading volume across WhiteBIT’s flagship BTC, ETH and WBT pairs increased more than fivefold, from $53 billion in 2020 to $276 billion in 2025. Meanwhile, bid-ask spreads across its major markets have narrowed approximately threefold since 2021, reflecting deeper liquidity.

WhiteBIT also serves more than 5,500 institutional clients, including funds, brokers and payment providers, through over 20 dedicated products and services. Businesses can access crypto liquidity, manage digital asset transactions and move between fiat currencies and cryptocurrencies through a single platform.

WhiteBIT’s eighth year brought significant regulatory milestones that strengthen the group’s international presence.

In June 2026, WhiteBIT EU secured authorisation under the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA) from Austria’s Financial Market Authority, establishing a regulatory foundation for providing crypto-asset services across the European Union.

In May, WhiteBIT launched a dedicated platform for users in the United Kingdom, expanding into another major financial market with demanding regulatory requirements. The company also joined Ghana’s regulatory sandbox in March, contributing to the development of the country’s digital asset regulatory framework.

These developments reflect WhiteBIT’s investment in compliance as a foundation for sustainable international growth.

The growth of the ecosystem is also reflected in WBT, WhiteBIT’s native coin, which reached an all-time high of nearly $88 in September 2026, up from its launch price of $1.62 in 2022.*The milestone reflects WBT’s strong long-term performance alongside the expansion of WhiteBIT and its ecosystem.

WBT’s role is also expanding beyond trading. In November, Whitechain transitioned into an Ethereum Layer 2 network built on the OP Stack in partnership with Optimism, with WBT used to pay transaction fees. Designed to support blockchain applications and financial services, Whitechain has already attracted interest from developers, with more than 140 teams applying to its Builders Program ahead of the network’s public launch planned for later in November.

For W Group, the next stage of growth will focus on connecting its businesses more closely and turning their combined capabilities into new products and services.

“Eight years ago, we started with one cryptocurrency exchange. Today, we’ve grown into an international group of 11 companies serving around 40 million users. But our ambition has never been simply to build more businesses. We want to connect them in ways that create real value — bringing traditional finance and digital assets closer together, making new technologies more accessible and opening opportunities across industries,” said Volodymyr Nosov, Founder and President of W Group.

Looking ahead, W Group aims to strengthen its presence in regulated markets, expand institutional financial services and accelerate blockchain infrastructure development. Its long-term vision is an interconnected ecosystem where banking, payments, digital assets and emerging technologies work together, making financial services more accessible to people and businesses worldwide.

Bitcoin (BTC) price continues to fall as the sell-off from the $86,000 - $87,000 region in October is gathering momentum. The sell-off has accelerated in recent days, and BTC price has slipped to roughly $61,900, moving closer to the next technical support level at $60,000.

The daily chart shows several concerning technical developments for Bitcoin. Shorter-term moving averages continue to fall below longer-term moving averages, forming a technical pattern commonly known as a death cross. The death cross has now formed twice with 100 and 200 EMAs, indicating a worsening technical setup for Bitcoin, commonly known as a double death cross.

Several key moving averages continue to cluster in the $75,000 - $76,000 region, adding resistance for Bitcoin price action.

Relative Strength Index (RSI) has started to move closer to the oversold region, indicating that momentum has started to slow for Bitcoin.

Taken together, this technical setup indicates that selling pressure for Bitcoin has been increasing on multiple time frames. We are monitoring $60,000 as a key support level. This level was also an area of interest for buyers during the June correction in Bitcoin.

Should BTC price continue to move lower and break out below $60,000, the next level of support to watch will be $58,000, followed by $56,000.

For Bitcoin price to reverse course and show signs of a meaningful short-term rebound, it will need to continue higher and break out above $64,000 - $65,000.

Breaking out above $68,000 would be a strong move that could help to stabilize Bitcoin in the short term. A positive move for Bitcoin would need to continue higher and reclaim several key moving averages. Until then, Bitcoin will continue to trade in a more bearish technical setup.

Bitcoin price action continues to move lower on the daily chart. All technical indicators on this chart continue to deteriorate, indicating that Bitcoin remains vulnerable to another leg lower before buyers can show signs of a robust short-term recovery.

"Rich Dad Poor Dad" author Robert Kiyosaki wrote on X on Nov. 20 that he is "most excited about Bitcoin's crash" and is "waiting to buy more." On the same day, Bitcoin was trading at $61,666, more than 50% below its October 2025 peak of about $126,000.

Gold fell 1.24% to $3,579 an ounce, and silver lost 0.95% to $42.42, according to TradingView data. The S&P 500 dropped 2.02% on the same day.

Kiyosaki started his post with a question. "CRASH: Good or Bad? Gold, silver, Bitcoin, crashing. Weak hands selling. Strong hands waiting to buy?" he wrote.

According to Kiyosaki, the reasons include "incompetence in FED, Banks, and Bond markets." He also wrote that America's debt is "only to grow bigger" as "Banksters steal our wealth via their system legally."

The author pointed to Bitcoin's fixed supply. There will be only 21 million BTC in total, and about 20 million coins have already been mined, Kiyosaki wrote. "As far as I know, there has never been a 'money' such as Bitcoin ever before," he added.

"With price of Bitcoin crashing, I can't wait to buy more coins… just because only 21 million are ever to be mined. It could be a 'nothing burger'…. or the best money I've ever spent," Kiyosaki wrote.

In late August, Kiyosaki said on podcasts that he owed creditors $1.2 billion. His ex-wife and business partner, Kim Kiyosaki, later said that the figure covered the loans of a partnership that owns about 1,500 rental units. "We have a lot of apartment houses with our partners," she said.

According to Kim Kiyosaki, Robert Kiyosaki's own share of the debt is $30 million to $60 million. Each of their real estate investments is held in a separate LLC. Robert Kiyosaki also commented on the debt at the time. "If it all comes to hell, you can talk to my attorney," he said.

In 2012, Kiyosaki's company Rich Global LLC filed for bankruptcy after a court ordered it to pay about $24 million.

#5198. OmenX announces $2 million in funding from Informed Ventures and launches on-demand 30-second Bitcoin predictions

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Toronto, November 19, 2026 – OmenX, a Base-native leveraged prediction market platform, today announced $2 million in funding from Informed Ventures alongside the launch of its on-demand, 30-second Bitcoin price prediction product.

The new product lets users predict whether Bitcoin’s price will rise or fall over the next 30 seconds, with each trade starting its own prediction window. A position opened at 10:00:12 runs until 10:00:42. Users can act when their view forms, with a full 30-second horizon, rather than adapting to the remaining time in a shared market round.

Featuring zero-slippage execution and rapid settlement, the product extends the familiar five- and fifteen-minute crypto prediction format to a shorter, individually timed experience. It adds to OmenX’s intraday offering, which spans prediction horizons from 30 seconds to 24 hours, depending on the market.

Beyond crypto, OmenX offers directional prediction markets linked to more than 100 global assets, including U.S. equities, futures, ETFs and indices. Its event markets also cover live sports and esports, with sports coverage spanning major football leagues, basketball, American football, ice hockey, baseball and UFC.

Leverage has been central to OmenX’s platform from the outset, allowing traders to amplify their exposure on supported event markets. The latest launch builds on that foundation while advancing a broader goal: making prediction markets a practical financial tool for retail users.

OmenX organizes the trading decision around a defined question: will an asset’s price be higher or lower at the end of a specified period? Users can express a directional view without purchasing the underlying asset, targeting an exact closing price or constructing an options position that requires decisions about strikes, implied volatility and time decay.

“Leverage has been part of OmenX from the start, but our ambition goes beyond adding leverage to prediction markets,” said James, founder and CEO of OmenX. “We want to make global markets easier to participate in. A trader should be able to take a view on Bitcoin, a stock or a sporting event and express it through a clear contract and a timeframe that fits their judgment.”

The platform’s emphasis on short, recurring markets provides faster feedback on trading decisions and can reduce the time capital remains committed to individual outcomes. OmenX plans to expand its coverage of traditional and crypto assets while deepening the trading experience across supported markets.

OmenX is a Base-native leveraged prediction market platform covering crypto, global financial assets, live sports and esports. Through defined outcomes, short settlement cycles and leverage on supported markets, OmenX is building a more accessible way to trade market views.

Learn more at omenx.com. Media contact James Zhang

#5197. Cardano’s $5M conference budget has a $1M problem — Details!

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

The Cardano [ADA] Treasury Foundation wants 25 million ADA to host 12 events in 2027. Its last $22 million proposal (to buy copper) barely got any votes at all.

Hence, the question — Will this one fare any better?

On 16th November, the Cardano Foundation filed a proposal to pull 24,995,775 ADA from the network’s treasury. The money would pay for Cardano’s presence at 12 crypto events next year.

Some of the biggest names on the circuit are on the list. Consensus in Miami, TOKEN2049 in both Singapore and New York, Web Summit in Lisbon, and India Blockchain Week in Bangalore.

The run kicks off in February with the Africa Tech Summit in Nairobi.

$2 million will go towards sponsorships and $1.06 million for booths and equipment. Travel is said to cost $702K, while side events will account for $695,000.

According to the Foundation, none of it covers salaries or profit. Whatever isn’t spent goes back to the treasury.

However, here’s what’s tricky. The Foundation priced ADA at $0.20 to reach its $5 million budget. ADA, however, was valued at $0.15 at press time. At that price, the request is worth about $3.85 million. That is a gap of over $1 million.

For the budget to work as planned, ADA needs to climb by almost 30%. Not impossible, but far from guaranteed.

DReps, the delegates who vote on treasury spending, have until 20th December to decide.

Will 25 million ADA move the price? Probably not. There are about 37.6 billion ADA in circulation. So, this withdrawal will merely be a drop in the ocean.

However, it’s worth pointing out that the chart had bigger problems at press time.

ADA fell from $0.25 in October to $0.155 following a price drop on the 14th.

Is a pause imminent? We might be in the early stages, yes. The RSI fell to 21 after that drop, with the same since climbing to 32, just crossing above its average. The OI has also recovered from about $145 million to $153.5 million. Finally, the funding rates were positive yesterday.

On the contrary, the Chaikin Money Flow was negative, implying that sellers might still have a slight edge.

#5196. BlackRock Records Largest Bitcoin Outflow in History

BlackRock, the leading asset management firm and Bitcoin’s largest ETF issuer, sparked discussions earlier today following a massive Bitcoin sale by the company.

The latest data showcased by SosoValue shows that the leading Bitcoin fund has witnessed massive single-day withdrawals from investors who have ventured into its Bitcoin investment product.

Earlier today, BlackRock sold over half a billion dollars’ worth of Bitcoin after its spot Bitcoin ETF, also known as iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), recorded a total of $541.08 million in net outflows.

This massive outflow has come as Bitcoin’s price decline continues to intensify, causing investors to aggressively pull their money out of the fund amid growing market fear.

While this marks the third time this week that BlackRock has recorded a net outflow amid persistent market volatility, it also marks the largest single-day outflow BlackRock has recorded since its launch.

Apparently, the record-breaking withdrawal that the fund just witnessed suggests that institutional and traditional investors are becoming less willing to retain their exposure to Bitcoin through asset managers, especially as Bitcoin’s price continues to slump further.

Although BlackRock has just suffered the largest withdrawal since it launched its Bitcoin investment product, the record outflow did not alter its dominance in the market.

Further data shows that the BlackRock spot Bitcoin ETF still boasts a massive $47.82 billion in assets under management, spotlighting its leadership in the Bitcoin ETF market.

This positions it far ahead of Fidelity, which ranks as the second-largest Bitcoin ETF with just $10.62 billion in net assets.

Hong Kong has just put Hyperliquid [HYPE] on its watchlist. And yet, traders don’t seem to be bothered.

In fact, on Hyperliquid itself, the action is only heating up now.

On Wednesday, Hong Kong’s Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) added Hyperliquid to its Alert List. The problem cited was that they don’t hold a licence to operate in the city.

The regulator’s entry covers two names; Hyperliquid and Hyperliquid Hong Kong. It also shared the exchange’s trading website. It is believed that the platform may be serving Hong Kong users, presenting itself as a local operator, or pitching its services to people in the city.

With this addition, the SFC’s list of suspicious crypto trading platforms has grown to 69 names now. At the time of writing, Hyperliquid hadn’t commented on the development.

Back in June, Singapore’s central bank placed Hyperliquid on its Investor Alert List which flags firms people might wrongly assume are regulated there. At the time, Hyperliquid’s response was simple — it never said it had a Singapore licence.

Now, there are two Asian financial hubs keeping an eye on the exchange.

While Hong Kong was flagging Hyperliquid, traders on the platform were busy betting on Anthropic.

On 18th November, the number of traders holding long positions on Anthropic perps hit a record 5,567.

A week ago, that figure was 2,926; nearly doubling in seven days. There were 1,996 short holders, with the same hinting at 2.8 longs for every short.

Most of that action was on Trade[XYZ]’s ANT market. According to Token Terminal, this alone accounted for 4,190 long holders,.

One caveat, though. These numbers count traders, not the size of their bets. And since the data adds up three markets, anyone trading on two of them gets counted twice.

The altcoin was trading at $67.66, at press time, following a hike of just 1% in the last 24 hours. Its price was still a long way from its late-October levels when it briefly climbed above $95. Since then, it’s been mostly downhill for the crypto.

There seemed to be some sign of a breather though. The RSI was below 30 during that drop. It has since come back to just nudging above its average.

The CMF at -0.06 suggested that sellers still had the upper hand, but the outflows were clearly weaker than earlier this month.

#5192. XRP Ledger Breaks Vote Stall on Bank-Style Lending: What It Unlocks for XRP Holders

Disclaimer: The opinions expressed by our writers are their own and do not represent the views of U.Today. The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. Conduct your own research by contacting financial experts before making any investment decisions. We believe that all content is accurate as of the date of publication, but certain offers mentioned may no longer be available.

Three XRP Ledger amendments linked to native lending have each gained two validator votes since Nov. 17, according to XRPScan data. As of Nov. 20, 2026, Single Asset Vault (XLS-65) had 25 votes, and Lending Protocol (XLS-66) and the LendingProtocolV1_1 patch had 24 votes each.

XRPScan data shows that LendingProtocolV1_1 has been up for a vote since Sept. 29, 2026, when it came with the v3.4.0 release. According to the patch's voting history, it had about 19 votes for most of October. It started to gain votes again in late October. XRP was trading at $0.96 on Friday.

Lending is built directly into the XRP Ledger's code, with no third-party smart contracts. According to Ripple, lenders deposit into a Single Asset Vault, and the Lending Protocol lets loan brokers use that capital "to issue loans and track repayments onchain."

The model is close to how banks lend. Loans have fixed terms and a repayment schedule, and credit brokers vet borrowers before the loans are issued. On Nov. 19, Clearpool showed the full lending flow on the XRPL Devnet with Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin. In the demo, "An approved lender funds a private vault, and a borrower accepts and repays a loan underwritten offchain by a broker," Clearpool wrote.

Through Single Asset Vault (XLS-65), XRP holders will be able to deposit their coins into shared liquidity pools, and institutional borrowers will take loans from those pools at a fixed rate. After the loan is repaid, "the lender redeems at a higher share price," according to the Clearpool demo.

The amendments still need more votes before they can activate. "An amendment needs more than 80% support, held for 14 days, to activate," XRPScan says on its amendment pages. For the current set of 35 validators, the site puts the threshold at "more than 80% of 35 votes, so 29 needed."

#5191. Scattered Spider Hacker Sentenced to 6 Years Over $11.6M in Stolen Crypto

Scattered Spider Hacker Sentenced to 6 Years Over $11.6M in Stolen Crypto

A Scottish hacker who was part of the Scattered Spider hacking collective has been sentenced to six years in U.S. federal prison for his role in a scheme that stole at least $11.6 million in crypto.

Tyler Robert Buchanan, 24, of Dundee, was sentenced to 72 months by a federal judge in Santa Ana, California, on Tuesday, the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Central District of California said. The judge set a restitution hearing for December 11. Buchanan began hacking as a teenager and was part of Scattered Spider, the group of young, English-speaking hackers blamed for a string of high-profile cyberattacks, the BBC reported.

British national sentenced to six years in federal prison for hacking into companies and stealing at least $11 million in virtual currency https://t.co/h7oprrXcVK

— US Attorney L.A. (@USAO_LosAngeles) November 18, 2026

Buchanan pleaded guilty in April to conspiracy to commit wire fraud and aggravated identity theft. At the time, prosecutors said the scheme had stolen at least $8 million in crypto. That figure has since risen to at least $11.6 million.

Between September 2021 and April 2023, Buchanan and his co-conspirators sent hundreds of phishing text messages to employees of at least a dozen companies, including telecoms, technology firms and crypto companies, according to the indictment and Buchanan's plea agreement. The messages linked to fake websites that captured employees' login details, which were sent to a Telegram channel run by Buchanan and another co-conspirator.

The group used information stolen from those companies to identify individual crypto holders, then carried out SIM swaps, tricking mobile carriers into moving victims' phone numbers to devices they controlled so they could intercept two-factor authentication codes and empty victims' wallets.

In the largest single theft, one victim lost $1.67 million in December 2022, according to the BBC. When authorities searched Buchanan's home in Scotland in April 2023, they found the names and addresses of numerous victims, and a text file containing crypto seed phrases and login details for one victim's account, prosecutors said.

"Those thefts had severe, life-altering consequences for many victims," prosecutors argued in a sentencing memo.

Buchanan is the fifth and final defendant to be sentenced in the case, which the Justice Department charged in November 2024. A Justice Department spokesperson confirmed at the time that the defendants were suspected members of Scattered Spider, the group behind high-profile attacks including the 2023 breach of MGM Resorts. Buchanan was arrested at Palma de Mallorca Airport in Spain in May 2024 while trying to board a private flight to Naples, the BBC reported, and has been in U.S. custody since April 2025.

His co-defendant Noah Urban, of Palm Coast, Florida, is serving 10 years in prison, while Ahmed Hossam Eldin Elbadawy and Evans Onyeaka Osiebo were each sentenced to 45 months, and Joel Martin Evans to two years.

U.S. authorities have continued to pursue alleged Scattered Spider members. In July, a 19-year-old suspect was extradited from Finland over an $8 million crypto ransom demand against a luxury jeweler.

The impact also seems to have spilled over into crypto, with the total market cap forming its third consecutive lower low at $2.08 trillion, a level last seen in early Q3.

In essence, ANT’s pre-IPO futures generated more than 2.4x SpaceX’s.

This highlights how much larger speculative interest in ANT was compared to SpaceX, setting a new record for pre-IPO trading activity on crypto platforms. However, the initial hype quickly turned into profit-taking, with ANT dropping 13% from its opening price. This shift in sentiment may have added to Bitcoin’s [BTC] selling pressure, especially as liquidation activity picked up alongside the broader market breakdown.

So, is Bitcoin’s latest breakdown the start of an overall deleveraging process in crypto markets? In other words, could IPO-driven volatility have accelerated long liquidations, forced overleveraged traders out of positions, and triggered a general market reset?

It looks like ANT’s futures activity on crypto platforms may have added to the selling pressure.

According to CoinGlass, over $700 million worth of positions have been liquidated in the last 24 hours. Of that amount, nearly $600 million was long positions, indicating that leveraged bulls have been badly hit by the correction. However, can this flush-out in Futures markets lead to a rebalance?

Worth mentioning here is the ongoing liquidity drain. In the last 30 days, $11.5 billion has left the stablecoin supply. That outflow is greater than it was in the aftermath of the Terra collapse in 2022. While many in the crypto market are looking at Bitcoin’s price movements, the real problem is the decreasing capital in crypto.

Why does this matter? Lower stablecoin supply means less available liquidity to support buying activity, which could keep pressure on Bitcoin and the broader market.

So, while ANT-related volatility may have contributed to market deleveraging, liquidity is still very poor for a sustained recovery. In this context, ANT’s IPO may have added to an already fragile market, while concerns around its valuation may also “continue” to create a risk-off sentiment in U.S. markets.

Against this backdrop, a drop in the total crypto market cap below $2 trillion cannot be ruled out.

ANT’s IPO may have added to Bitcoin’s fear and increased crypto selling.

Weak liquidity could keep pressure on crypto, putting the $2 trillion market cap at risk.

#5185. Standard Chartered and OCBC test dollar payments in minutes without traditional banking cutoffs

The bank says eligible clients can move funds in near real time, while a separate OCBC and StraitsX trial tested payments between banks.

Standard Chartered said Nov. 19 that eligible clients can now transfer tokenized deposits, bank balances recorded on a digital ledger, between Singapore and Hong Kong in near real time.

That gives corporate treasury teams a way to shift cash between entities in the same group on the bank’s own blockchain.

Meanwhile, a separate trial with OCBC and StraitsX tested payments across two banks’ networks.

The bank’s Singapore expansion covers treasury and investment transactions that use commercial bank deposits. Standard Chartered listed the Singapore dollar, Hong Kong dollar, US dollar, euro, offshore Chinese yuan and British pound among the supported currencies.

It named corporate treasurers, banks, investment platforms, and digital asset businesses as potential users, but detailed eligibility criteria and operating hours for the route remain unspecified.

The bank disclosed round-the-clock settlement when it launched its Hong Kong service Nov. 2. That schedule applies to tokenized deposit transactions settled between participating banks in central bank money through the Hong Kong Monetary Authority’s EnsembleTX infrastructure.

On Nov. 19, Standard Chartered, Singapore bank OCBC and payment infrastructure provider StraitsX said they had completed a controlled trial under the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s BLOOM initiative.

The trial completed US dollar payments across the banks’ separate deposit networks outside conventional cutoffs. Participants said the test showed how payments could move within minutes, including compliance checks, liquidity checks, and settlement.

The trial partners, StraitsX, OCBC and Standard Chartered, explain that each tokenized deposit remains a claim on the bank that issued it. Banks can use different platforms and standards for their deposits, so interbank payments need a way to coordinate settlement across those systems.

Standard Chartered opened a transfer route for eligible clients between Singapore and Hong Kong. A separate trial tested US dollar payments between two banks’ deposit networks.

Standard Chartered’s release gives no schedule for the live route. The trial partners say a commercial service remains subject to approvals and operational assessments.

StraitsX coordinated payment instructions and transaction details and helped with screening and settlement. The shared infrastructure handled the payment process across both networks, from initiation to confirmation.

The partners reported that this setup reduced the need for bilateral prefunding, where banks set aside money in advance to cover payments.

A commercial service based on the trial would still depend on regulatory engagement, participant approval, legal documentation, and operational risk assessments, the partners said. They also flagged settlement finality, meaning when a payment becomes irrevocable.

Banks would need to work out who is responsible for each step, how to screen for financial crime and how to keep enough funds available for payments to settle.

#5183. AI Will Make the Next 12 Months 'a Slaughterhouse' for Crypto Security: Anchorage Exec

AI Will Make the Next 12 Months 'a Slaughterhouse' for Crypto Security: Anchorage Exec

Crypto companies face a wave of AI-powered attacks over the coming year, on top of an already relentless threat from North Korea, security leaders warned at Solana's Breakpoint conference in London.

"The next 12 months are going to be absolutely brutal," said Diogo Mónica, co-founder of crypto bank Anchorage Digital. "They're going to be a slaughterhouse."

Over the past three to six months, AI systems have gone from finding vulnerabilities to building full exploits and carrying out every step of an attack on their own, Mónica said on a panel chaired by Gordon Corera, co-host of The Rest Is Classified podcast. Aggressive hacking tools now let anyone with no security knowledge simply tell a model to "please hack this website," he said.

Michael Coates, chief information security officer at the Solana Foundation, said AI has "dramatically lowered the cost and the barrier to hacking." Projects that once escaped attention will now be targeted opportunistically, he said.

North Korea remains the biggest threat to crypto firms, Coates said in a separate presentation. More than $13 billion in crypto has been stolen over the past decade, over $7.5 billion of it this year alone, with some $6 billion drained in a single breach: last month's hack of Binance, which the FBI has blamed on North Korea. "This is how they fund their programs in North Korea," he said.

Coates described the Binance attack as a chain of familiar tactics. A developer downloaded poisoned software from a sponsored search result, and an engineer later took a job interview on a work device and downloaded software as part of it. That gave the attackers a foothold to move through the network and reach signing services, which they used to authorize malicious transactions rather than steal the keys themselves, he said.

Fake job interviews are a "telltale tactic of North Korea," he said, along with poisoned tools and deepfake video calls. North Korean hackers have stolen $400 million using deepfake calls alone. When North Korean operatives can't get hired directly, they use people in the U.S. to take jobs on their behalf, then connect remote keyboards and mice so attackers can access the company's network, Mónica said.

The U.S. Treasury recently sanctioned 11 people over just such a North Korean IT worker scheme. Anchorage now onboards new staff in person at its U.S. office, Mónica added, and every employee works on a locked-down Chromebook, logging into remote machines for development, which he said removes 90% to 95% of its corporate attack surface.

Coates pointed teams to STRIDE, a free security framework the Solana Foundation launched in the spring. It sets out 18 core controls tailored for crypto, and protocols covering more than 74% of DeFi's total value locked on Solana, including 10 of the top 11, have gone through it, he said. The foundation is also using AI to reverse-engineer newly launched programs and find flaws before attackers do, which he said has prevented more than $5 million in potential losses in the past month.

Both executives warned against basic mistakes. Connecting email inboxes to AI agents invites prompt injection attacks, Mónica said, while Coates urged teams to "protect the keys," using hardware security keys for logins and properly configured multisig wallets, with plans for key rotation and loss. "That's where we see the attackers going," Coates said. "They're getting the entry points through the basics. They're pivoting around to get the keys, and that's where they're unleashing their fury."

As of Nov. 20, Shiba Inu (SHIB) is about $10 million in market capitalization short of overtaking Bittensor (TAO) for the No. 33 spot in CoinMarketCap's global crypto ranking. TAO has a market cap of $2.18 billion at a price of $186.41, and SHIB has $2.17 billion at $0.000003691 and ranks No. 34.

A gain of about 0.5% in SHIB's price, with TAO's price unchanged, would be enough for the meme coin to take Bittensor's place in the ranking.

TAO is the token of the Bittensor AI network, and Digital Currency Group (DCG) founder Barry Silbert has been one of its most vocal backers. Silbert also runs Yuma, a DCG company that builds on Bittensor.

At Fortune's Brainstorm Tech conference in September 2025, Silbert said that Bittensor was the thing he had gotten most excited about since Bitcoin. "I want to open up the development and the access to AI, and Bittensor is enabling that," he said at the time. Silbert also said that Bittensor is building a "world wide web of intelligence."

SHIB spent most of the year in the red. The meme coin rose about 25% in January, and it has not been in positive territory since February. By Nov. 20, SHIB had lost about 50% since the start of the year, and it fell 13.79% over the past week.

Shiba Inu developer Mazrael responded to the drop on X on Nov. 17. "1 SHIB is always 1 SHIB," he wrote in reply to a user who pointed to the falling price.

#5181. Pony AI’s robotaxi fares surge nearly 400% but its operating losses barely budge

Pony.ai says fares covered the vehicle costs it tracks in Guangzhou and Shenzhen, leaving the profitability of individual rides unclear.

Pony.ai’s robotaxi fare revenue nearly quintupled year over year in the September quarter, while the company-wide operating loss narrowed to $68.7 million from $69.7 million.

In its Nov. 18 filing, Pony.ai said fare revenue rose nearly 400% year over year. Revenue from its broader robotaxi services business grew 165.4% to $17.8 million from $6.7 million, helped by both passenger fares and higher vehicle deliveries to joint deployments in China and overseas.

In a November service update, separate from its September-quarter figures, Pony.ai said the previously separate operating zones in central Guangzhou and Nansha formed one contiguous area of more than 1,000 square kilometers as of Nov. 17.

Riders can use its PonyPilot app to book trips between Nansha and central Guangzhou, where Pony.ai holds a citywide commercial permit. The area it measured in November covers the connected operating zones where the company says those bookings are available.

CEO James Peng said PonyPilot now lets riders book across Nansha, Haizhu, Tianhe, Huangpu and Panyu. He said the wider network had increased trip distances and the average price per ride in Guangzhou.

On the November earnings call, CFO Leo Wang reported that Pony.ai’s fleets in Guangzhou and Shenzhen had earned enough in fares to more than cover the vehicle costs Pony.ai includes in its calculation.

Pony.ai starts with fares after discounts and refunds, then deducts vehicle depreciation, charging, wages for remote and ground staff, cleaning and maintenance, insurance, parking and communications.

Wang said depreciation accounts for about half of those costs. It covers the vehicle, including the battery and the hardware used to drive it autonomously.

The company said premiums per seventh-generation robotaxi fell 19% from a year earlier at renewal, giving no profit margin for an individual ride.

The gap was visible in Spectra’s market overview on Nov. 19, which shows that its later pools mature on Dec. 31 and March 31, 2027. The first question for Spectra holders at maturity is which token the position can deliver on Flare.

Firelight takes FXRP, the representation of XRP on the Flare network, and issues stXRP shares in its vault. On Spectra, a buyer can purchase a principal token at a discount and redeem it at maturity.

This November series has its own market on Flare, which lists stXRP as the default input or output and FXRP as the underlying asset.

At maturity, Spectra holders can open their positions to see the available redemption token and estimated proceeds. Spectra’s redemption guide shows the underlying payout is normally close to one unit per principal token, with a lower rate possible if the strategy suffers a loss.

Spectra’s contracts also support redemption in the interest-bearing token. In that case, the output also depends on the conversion rate. For this series, the market labels identify the two assets, and the position’s redemption quote determines the available route and amount.

The pool’s $2.8 million counts the value on both sides of the market, stXRP and principal tokens. The amount redeemed at maturity depends on the principal token holders present and the rate the contract applies.

Spectra’s Nov. 19 overview at 12:29 UTC showed $2.77M, $51K and $13K in two-sided liquidity for the three listed Firelight stXRP pools.

Source: Spectra markets overview · Spectra Nov. 26 market · Spectra pool list

Spectra’s overview showed fixed rates of 5.21% for November, 7.56% for December, and 8.01% for March. The yield earned between purchase and maturity depends on the price paid and the time left. A rollover is a new trade, so its terms depend on what a later pool quotes for that order.

The December market held roughly $36,400 in principal tokens and $14,400 in stXRP as of Nov. 19. A buyer taking principal tokens from the pool would have to price that trade against the available inventory.

A holder who receives stXRP can swap the shares for FXRP at a market price. The amount received depends on the trade quote, which can differ from the Firelight vault’s share value.

Both the swap and the rollover depend on what the market will fill for a given amount of stXRP. Meanwhile, Firelight’s unstaking process records the share value in FXRP when the holder requests a withdrawal and ends reward accrual at that point.

The FXRP becomes withdrawable at the end of the next coverage period, currently 30 to 60 days after the request, and the holder must submit a second transaction to claim it. During the wait, claims tied to capital-backed coverage can still reduce the payout.

FAssets redemption burns FXRP on Flare and has an agent send native XRP to the holder’s XRP Ledger address.

The redemption request sets the payment deadline, and applicable fees reduce the amount the agent sends.

#5178. XRP Faces Severe Supply Shortage on Binance

The price of XRP has continued to slump to deeper levels amid the prolonged market volatility. However, recent onchain data has shown an unexpected trend in exchange activity.

According to the latest data from crypto analytics platform Cryptoquant, XRP is currently facing a severe supply shortage on the world’s largest crypto exchange, Binance.

According to the data, XRP’s Supply Shortage Index on Binance has surged to 2.4 as of November 19 despite the asset’s extreme price weakness in recent days.

Notably, the data further shows that the metric has surpassed the previous reading of 2.09 recorded on July 6, marking a five-month high in XRP’s supply shortage index.

It is important to note that readings above +2 are a strong indication of severely tightened supply, which means that the amount of XRP available on the exchange has decreased significantly.

While negative readings often mean the opposite, this means that XRP has witnessed a sharp reversal from the supply level seen on September 27.

At the time, the index stood at -1.5 while XRP traded above $1.50, signaling an abundance of XRP on Binance. This means that more tokens were available for trading during the period, which potentially added to selling pressure.

While that is no longer the case, the latest data shows that the XRP supply index has jumped by 3.9 points in just 53 days, moving from supply abundance to severe supply tightness in just about two months.

This typically suggests that XRP is being aggressively moved out of exchanges despite its prolonged price weakness, potentially driving a rebound in the demand for XRP, which could eventually trigger a price recovery.

#5176. 'Doomed From the Start': President Trump's Meme Coin Hits New Lows After Midterms

'Doomed From the Start': President Trump's Meme Coin Hits New Lows After Midterms

President Trump's official meme coin has reached new lows since he suffered a major blow in the U.S. midterm elections. The token has dropped almost 40% since election day, and analysts warn that new congressional scrutiny could push it lower.

Over the weekend, the TRUMP coin touched $0.896, marking the lowest point the token had ever stooped. It has since bumped 8%, sitting at $0.965, which is still down almost 40% from election day and 98.7% from its all-time high of $73.43, set the day after it launched, per Decrypt data.

Luke Nolan, senior researcher at CoinShares, told Decrypt the midterms "added pressure to an already struggling token." Trading volume increased around the vote, and he believes some traders had bet on a Republican surprise win. He said there was a "visible unwind" that led to a "sharp drawdown" after the election results rolled out.

"Democrats take both chambers in January and plan to use their subpoena power on his crypto ventures. His net approval rating has almost never been lower," Max Shannon, senior associate at Bitwise Europe, told Decrypt. "It is still possible this continues to decline and, therefore, has a negative effect on these Trump-affiliated assets."

Other Trump-linked assets have also taken a hit. Since the election, World Liberty Financial's WLFI token has dropped 7.5%, per Decrypt data, and shares of the Trump Media & Technology Group have dropped 32%.

Trump launched TRUMP on January 17, 2025, three days before his second inauguration, which Shannon described as "close to the peak of his popularity." Since then, the coin has faced significant scrutiny over how much the President and his family have profited from it. (The First Lady following suit and launching her own meme coin didn't help matters.)

The president’s crypto ventures also became a sticking point for the Clarity Act, a bill that aimed to provide a formal legal structure for most cryptocurrency activity. Democrats scrutinized the Trump family's involvement in the crypto industry, which profited them more than $1 billion in a year.

A July draft would have barred public officials and employees, along with their spouses, from issuing or sponsoring digital assets while in office. That draft didn’t extend to officials’ children, including Don Jr. and Eric Trump, and the provision would have expired in January 2029.

The bill failed a key Senate procedural vote in September. Patrick Witt, former executive director of the President’s Council of Advisers for Digital Assets, later said the “political issue of ethics really consumed everything else.”

TRUMP has "no value accrual, and it has been left in the dust of this narrative," Shannon said. "Google Trends shows searches for $TRUMP essentially flatlining since June 2025."

Nolan agreed, saying the coin’s appeal was "largely speculative," with no clear link between holding it and sharing in any underlying business success. The most it offered, he said, was the exclusive dinner to the top holders, which was both popular and controversial, depending on who you asked.

"In my view, that was just an attempt to prop up the token without actually creating any long-term demand for it," he said.

Interest in these dinners has dried up too. Ahead of the third gala scheduled for the event of the month, 185 holders of the token were invited to register, but only 130 wallets showed on the final leaderboard. Those wallets held a combined $8.6 billion worth of TRUMP, according to Reuters, which is a 94% decline from the first dinner.

Then there's the "unappealing" token supply structure, Nolan said. The majority of tokens were allocated to Trump-linked entities and are being slowly unlocked, which means demand needs to keep growing to soak up newly injected supply.

"That is a difficult position for an asset whose main attraction is attention around one individual," he said.

And what happens when Trump loses power? He has said he "would love" to serve a third term, but that remains unconstitutional—so the clock is ticking on his presidency.

"I think overall Trump leaving office probably means the token continues its gradual decline," Nolan told Decrypt. "Any big Trump headlines probably make it experience the same dead cat bounces (sharp rallies) we have seen it have during short periods of time."

Shannon thinks Trump doesn't even need to lose power for the token to keep going down. He said that it is "incredibly unlikely" that the token reclaims its highs, as it would require it to boost 82x, too many investors have been burned, and the majority of the supply is still to be unlocked.

"I think the meme coin was doomed from the start, and like with most meme coins, creating long-term demand is a Sisyphean task," Nolan told Decrypt.

#5175. Bitcoin Shows Unprecedented Weakness, Price Hits 4.5-Month Low

Bitcoin (BTC), the world’s largest cryptocurrency, is flashing a major, ‘scary’ technical signal that was absent even during its last major crashes in February and June 2026.

The flagship coin has crashed to a fresh 4.5-month low amid persistent institutional outflows totaling billions from cryptocurrency exchange-traded funds (ETFs).

$BTC hasn't formed a higher high for 16 consecutive days now. This didn't even happen during the Feb 2026 and June 2026 crashes. https://t.co/I6IPmdueEc

Bitcoin has failed to form a higher high for the past 16 days. This is a very long stretch, one that was absent during Bitcoin’s February and June crashes.

A higher high, in the context of technical analysis, is formed when an asset’s price reaches a new high point above its previous swing high. The absence of higher highs signals that buyers are having a hard time taking back control of the market.

The latest Bitcoin price action adds further to concerns surrounding the future of the flagship cryptocurrency.

Earlier today, BTC crashed to $61,225, its lowest price point in around four and a half months.

Bitcoin's failure to create higher highs despite several attempts to recover shows that selling pressure remains quite high.

Nevertheless, this technical pattern of 16 days without a higher high does not necessarily spell more pain for Bitcoin. If the cryptocurrency can decisively push above recent resistance zones, it may be a sign that buyers are starting to make a comeback.

Bitcoin is facing persistent withdrawals of huge amounts of money from U.S.-based spot Bitcoin ETFs.

BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) witnessed its biggest-ever daily net outflow on Nov. 19.

The crypto fund suffered a whopping $541.1 million in net withdrawals on the day. At the same time, total net outflows from U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs amounted to around $582.3 million across the entire market.

More alarmingly, the fresh wave of withdrawals brings cumulative net outflows from U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs to around $3.47 billion so far this November.

The ETFs have seen negative net flows on 12 of the first 14 trading days of the month.

#5173. Circle and Trump-linked crypto firm hit with court freeze order after Binance’s $6.3 billion hack

An Abu Dhabi court orders Circle and 17 firms to maintain freezes on crypto linked to Binance's theft ahead of a Dec. 1 hearing.

An Abu Dhabi court has ordered Circle and 17 other companies to keep tokens linked to Binance’s Oct. 29 theft frozen while the exchange tries to recover them.

Binance disclosed the order on Nov. 18 and said some issuers, exchanges and other partners ask for a court order before they will release or transfer assets they have frozen.

The exchange said the order from the Abu Dhabi Global Market Courts helps open that route, describing ongoing efforts to trace the stolen funds and giving no details of any transfer under the order.

The named firms include Circle, which issues USDC, and World Liberty Financial, the company behind USD1.

Reports noted that the firms must maintain the freezes pending further proceedings and cannot lend, swap, or mix the affected tokens with other assets.

The court did not accuse the firms of wrongdoing, and Dec. 1 is scheduled to consider whether to keep the injunction in place and on what terms.

The injunction covers specific assets Binance claimed are tied to the theft, and said it is still tracing the stolen crypto and taking legal steps to reclaim it. A transfer for firms seeking a court order depends on whether they have authority to release the specific balances they have frozen.

Tether falls outside the order covering the 18 firms, and the company said on Nov. 2 it had frozen more than $1.5 billion tied to the theft.

A spokesperson said Tether would work directly with Binance to reissue the tokens, in consultation with the relevant authorities.

The Abu Dhabi order directs 18 firms to maintain freezes. Tether says it will work separately with Binance on reissuing USDT.

The Abu Dhabi order follows earlier US court action. On Nov. 12, the US Justice Department said it had obtained court authority to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion in stolen crypto. That was part of more than $2.7 billion that US authorities and private firms had helped freeze.

In its Nov. 3 incident report, Binance estimated that about $6.3 billion in digital assets were affected and about $2.85 billion was frozen or intercepted, subject to reconciliation and market prices.

The separate disclosures do not establish how much the figures overlap or how much Binance can ultimately recover. Binance says it absorbed the financial impact on customers while continuing to pursue the stolen assets.

Shiba Inu’s layer-2 network, Shibarium, is experiencing a major slowdown as daily network activity has fallen to three-digit figures (fewer than 1,000 transactions), hitting lows not seen in months.

Shibarium processed 546 transactions, according to Shibariumscan data, marking a slower period for the layer-2 network after activity spiked to a high of 6,370 on October 31, 2026. Transaction activity declined afterward, and the decline intensified amid the sell-off that hit the market in recent weeks.

The latest figures suggest that fewer transactions are taking place across Shibarium compared with periods of stronger activity. The key question now is whether Shibarium can regain momentum in the coming weeks.

According to the latest figures shared by Etherscan SHIB, an X account dedicated to providing updates on the SHIB ecosystem, the cryptocurrency added 236 new on-chain holders in a single day, taking its total past the 1.7 million milestone.

"Shibarium has more holders than those you listed, though. But yeah. Well, there are also 1.4 million holders of Binance-pegged SHIB on BNB. But that's not actually CCIP SHIB; it is a peg," Mazrael wrote.

#5170. Coinbase opens crypto options in a market that accounted for just 2% of Deribit’s trading

Coinbase brings Deribit options to non-US users as USDC-settled contracts account for just 2% of the exchange’s options turnover.

Coinbase has opened a portion of Deribit’s options market to eligible customers outside the US, with contracts in Coinbase Advanced settling in USDC and falling into a product category that accounted for about 2% of Deribit’s October options turnover.

In two matched calls sampled on Nov. 19, USDC contracts had narrower spreads, while coin-settled contracts offered buyers more size at the best price.

On the same day, Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong announced on X that crypto options were live for non-US users.

The Coinbase Advanced options guide names Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, Avalanche, Hyperliquid, and XRP. All six use linear contracts, where traders pay the premium in USDC and in-the-money positions ultimately settle in the same stablecoin.

Coinbase directs customers to check eligibility in the app and complete derivatives onboarding where the service is offered. Coinbase had described a phased rollout in its earlier integration guidance.

The options rollout follows Coinbase’s Oct. 1 migration of its International Exchange (ICE) business to Deribit. The latest change lets eligible Coinbase Advanced users trade options from their existing Coinbase account, including through the app, on the infrastructure that already powers their international perpetuals.

Deribit’s October turnover report puts USDC options at $1.35 billion of $68.6 billion in total reported options turnover, or 1.97%. The BTC- and ETH-settled categories accounted for about $67.25 billion combined.

Deribit reports the inverse categories in dollar terms even though the contracts settle in their underlying coins.

October turnover in billions of U.S. dollars was 58.71 for BTC-settled options, 8.53 for ETH-settled options and 1.35 for USDC-settled options across assets.

Source: Monthly Statistics · · Linear contracts · · Inverse contracts

The USDC category covers multiple assets, so 1.97% describes activity for the venue’s full linear category before the announcement. The price and size a customer can trade depend on the orders available for the individual strike and expiration.

CryptoSlate sampled two Nov. 27 calls on Deribit between 20:11:50 and 20:12:36 UTC on Nov. 19, matching underlying asset, strike and expiration across settlement currencies. In both cases, the USDC book had the narrower quoted gap between the highest bid and lowest ask. The coin-settled book showed more size at the price a buyer could take.

For the $64,000 Bitcoin call, the USDC book showed a 25 USDC spread and 10 BTC of underlying exposure offered at the best ask. The BTC-settled book showed a spread equivalent to $31.03 and 25.9 BTC available at its best ask.

For the $1,800 Ethereum call, the USDC book showed a 0.80 USDC spread and 150 ETH at the best ask. Its ETH-settled counterpart showed a spread equivalent to $0.88 and 1,642 ETH offered at its best ask.

The size advantage flipped for sellers trading at the best bid. At that price, buyers were seeking 20.01 BTC and 116.1 ETH of exposure in the USDC books, compared with 12.8 BTC and 29 ETH in the coin-settled books.
